curseluckshield.text: Grants the Fateweaving ability. Anyone striking the unit will have their fate rewritten and suffer from misfortunes for the next few rounds of battle. The effect can be resisted with a successful Magic Resistance check. The penetration bonus makes the effect harder to resist.

custommagic.text: Gives a chance for another magic skill to the active monster. The path mask must be a number from Table 18 or a sum of multiple masks from this table. Chance should be a number from 1 to 100. Use this command multiple times for many random picks. E.g. use path mask 384 and chance 50 to give a commander a 50% chance of getting one level higher in Fire or Air magic. A chance of more than 100% creates a linked random (getting two or more levels of the same random path from one random pick like e.g. King of the Deep). For example, a 200% random chance means +2 levels in the path. This is displayed in the unit’s random magic information. NOTE: Using only a random priest level in a #custommagic mask causes the mod to crash. It is highly recommended not to use random priest levels unless you know exactly what you are doing to avoid problems.

damagerev.text: The monster has the Damage Reversal ability. Any creature that hits the monster must make a magic resistance check or suffer the damage itself instead of harming the target. Strength must be at least one and strength minus one is the penalty to the MR check. Use strength 1 for standard damage reversal with no penalty.

darkpower.text: The monster will get stat increases in darkness. Only active in combat.

darkvision.text: Gives monster darkvision, lessening penalties for fighting under darkness. Use value 100 for perfect darkvision.

deadhp.text: Number of HP gained per corpse eaten.

deathbanish.text: Whoever strikes the killing blow against this monster is banished to another plane. -11=The Void, -12=The Inferno, -13=Kokytos

deathcurse.text: When this monster dies, the unit that strikes the killing blow is cursed.

deathdisease.text: The monster bursts in a cloud of disease ridden fumes when it dies, infecting its killer and anyone nearby with disease.

deathfire.text: The monster erupts in a fiery explosion when it dies, inflicting 10 AP fire damage to everyone in the area of effect.

deathgrab.text: The monster erupts in a earth grip explosion when it dies, inflicting earth grip to everyone in the area of effect.

deathparalyze.text: The monster erupts in a paralyzing explosion on death, forcing everyone in the area of effect to make a MR check or become paralyzed.

deathpoison.text: The monster bursts in a cloud of poison when it dies, infecting its killer and anyone nearby with poison (str 2 poison cloud).

deathpower.text: The monster will get stat increases or decreases depending on the Death scale.

deathrange.text: Death magic cast by the monster have increased range.

deathrec.text: The monster is cheaper to recruit if there are Death scales in the province. Works identically to #chaosrec. Growth scales do not affect the price.

deathshock.text: The monster erupts in a shock explosion when it dies, inflicting capped 1 AN shock damage to everyone in the area of effect.

deathslime.text: The monster erupts in a slime explosion when it dies, inflicting slime (water breathers immune) to everyone in the area of effect.

decscale.text: Decreases the selected scale by one point per turn to a maximum of -3 / 3. This command functions as #incscale for the opposite scales.

def.text: The basic defense skill of the monster. A normal human soldier has 10.

defector.text: The monster has a chance to become independent if owned by a player. The Unfettered form of the Eater of the Dead uses this mechanic. This command only affects commanders.

descr.text: This is the text information that is displayed when you view the monster stats.

deserter.text: A commander with this attribute has chance of deserting each month.

digest.text: The monster digests any swallowed creatures. Swallowed creatures take <dmg> damage every combat round until dead or until the monster that swallowed them is killed.

diseasecloud.text: Monster is surrounded by a disease cloud. Standard size is 6. The disease cloud adds the Plague Carrier icon to the monster.

diseaseres.text: Protects a unit when diseased. Value is the chance of not being negatively affected by the disease each month.

divinebeing.text: This monster functions like a pretender god, but it is not the actual pretender. It will have stats depending on dominion, cannot become prophet, cannot be charmed and has no upkeep cost. This command is used for intelligent and significant mounts of pretenders.

divineins.text: There can only be a number of divinely inspired researchers per province equal to the dominion strength in that province. Any extra divinely inspired researchers have their research value ignored. The monks of Man use this mechanic.

djinn.text: Use this for djinns with a humanoid body, but no lower part.

doheal.text: Unit heals normally despite not usually being able to heal.

domimmortal.text: This monster is dominion immortal like a Phoenix.

dompower.text: The monster will get stat increases or decreases depending on the strength of the dominion in the province.

domrec.text: This monster can only be recruited if the dominion value of the province is at least this high.

domshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when inside a friendly dominion.

domsummon.text: Summons a number of monsters each month spent inside friendly dominion. The amount summoned is a dominion strength sided open ended die roll.

doomhorror.text: Monsters with this tag are used as doom horrors. All horrors automatically gain spirit sight.

douse.text: This monster gets a blood magic bonus when searching for blood slaves. Works like a Sanguine Dousing Rod (this item has a bonus of 1).

dragonlord.text: This monster will receive extra units when summoning Drakes of different kind.

drainimmune.text: The monster is immune to the effects of Drain scale like the Master Smiths of Ulm. There is no research penalty from Drain scale and in combat the fatigue costs of spells are not increased by the Drain scale. The monster gains all normal bonuses from an increased Magic scale.

drake.text: The monster is a drake and is affected by the Dragon Master ability.

drawsize.text: The value indicates how many percent larger size the sprite should be drawn at. A negative value means it will be draw at a smaller size than normal.

dread.text: Like fear, but negated by true sight.

dungeon.text: The monster is a suitable encounter in a dungeon.

earthelementals.text: Gives a size bonus to summoned earth elementals.

earthrange.text: Earth magic cast by the monster have increased range.

elegist.text: The monster is more effective than its normal priest level when calling a god or disciple back from death. The Elegist value is added to its priest level when performing this action.

elementgems.text: This monster produces a number of magic gems each month. They are of a single random type of elemental gem.

elementrange.text: Elemental magic (Fire, Air, Water, Earth) cast by the monster have increased range.

enc.text: The basic encumbrance of the monster. Normal humans have 3 and undead beings or machines have 0. Monsters with 0 encumbrance never get exhausted by fighting, only spellcasting.

enchantedblood.text: Gets points bonus to MR and heals about 0.5 HP per combat round. Also stops bleeding quickly.

enchrebate10.text: The monster will be 10 gold cheaper to recruit when this enchantment is active.

enchrebate100.text: The monster will be 100 gold cheaper to recruit when this enchantment is active.

enchrebate20.text: The monster will be 20 gold cheaper to recruit when this enchantment is active.

enchrebate25p.text: The monster will be 25 percent cheaper to recruit when this enchantment is active.

enchrebate50.text: The monster will be 50 gold cheaper to recruit when this enchantment is active.

enchrebate50p.text: The monster will be 50 percent cheaper to recruit when this enchantment is active.

enchrebate75.text: The monster will be 75 gold cheaper to recruit when this enchantment is active.

end.text: Always use this command at the end of modifying or creating a monster.

entangle.text: Anyone striking this monster may get entangled.

ethereal.text: The monster is ethereal. Non-magical weapons have only 25% chance of harming the monster when they hit, but when they do, they inflict full damage unless mitigated by another ability. Ethereal monsters can pass through walls during the storming of a fortress.

expertleader.text: Leadership value 150. Commanded units have a morale modifier of +2 for up to 4 squads and -1 for every additional squad.

expertmagicleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 150 magic beings. This is a very rare ability that only most magic beings possess.

expertundeadleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 150 undead beings. This is a rare ability that usually only demons or undead beings possess.

extralives.text: Will get dominion times this value amount of scar souls (extra lives).

eyeloss.text: Anyone striking this monster may lose an eye.

eyes.text: Sets the number of eyes for a monster. Number of eyes must be at least one unless the monster is #blind. The number of eyes affects how easily a monster goes blind by battle afflictions.

fallpower.text: The monster has increased hit points in autumn and lowered hit points in spring.

falsearmy.text: The monster creates the false impression of greater numbers than there really are. Enemy scouting reports will inflate the size of the army by <value> units.

falseregen.text: Heals false damage by this amount of points per combat round.

falsesupply.text: A monster with this ability produces extra false supplies.

farsail.text: Commander will be able to sail further if it can sail.

farthronekill.text: This monster will automatically destroy thrones in the same province, even if they are protected by a fort. Part is the percentage part that will be destroyed each turn, 100 means it will be destroyed in a single turn.

fastcast.text: Affects the spell casting time for commanders. Speedup 100=half time, 200=one third time, -50=double time.

faysummon.text: This monster will receive extra units when summoning fay folks of different kinds.

fear.text: This monster is very fearsome. A high value indicates higher fear. The standard value is 5. Death magic increases the fear value. The monster lowers the morale of enemy units in <value> squares around it. Affected squares are randomly determined. Units with Death magic 5 gain Fear even without this command.

fearofflood.text: Morale penalty when it is raining.

female.text: Being female is a minor advantage that makes you immune to being charmed by the Succubus. Commanders with this tag get feminine names.

fireelementals.text: Gives a size bonus to summoned fire elementals.

firepower.text: The monster will get stat increases or decreases depending on the Heat scale.

firerange.text: Fire magic cast by the monster have increased range.

fireres.text: Grants fire resistance to the monster. A value of 5 or more protects the monster from the fatigue effects of a heat aura.

fireshield.text: Anyone striking this monster will take <damage> points of armor piercing fire damage. Standard damage for fire shields is 8. Fire magic increases the amount of damage.

firstshape.text: This monster will change shape to its first shape when it feels ok. Werewolves have this ability in their wolf shapes. Monster nbr can be negative for montags.

fixedname.text: Gives a fixed name to a monster if it is a commander. Useful for giving specific names to heroes.

fixedresearch.text: The monster produces this amount of research even without magic skills.

fixforgebonus.text: Gem reduction when forging items. The value is in absolute numbers of gems, not in percent like the other forgebonus. This is the default forgebonus mechanic.

float.text: The monster floats in the air and can cross rivers. It is also immune to earthquakes and other effects that only affect ground bound monsters.

flying.text: This monster can fly. To be able to fly in a storm, the monster must also be #stormimmune. The monster can cross rivers. It can also cross mountain passes if it is not cold in the provinces the pass connects.

foolscouts.text: The monster creates the false impression of uniformity in its own army. Enemy scouting reports will perceive the army to only contain one type of troop. The reported troop type is usually the most common troop type present.

forcess.text: Usually being soul slayed will prevent any shape change or second shapes to save the victim. This command makes sure that the shape change takes place even if the target got soul slayed.

foreignshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when moving out of its home province.

forestshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when moving from a non-forest province to a forest province.

forestsurvival.text: Monster has the Forest Survival skill. Forest terrain does not hinder movement.

forgebonus.text: Makes it cheaper to create magic items.

formationfighter.text: A formation fighter is well drilled in using tight formations and can fit more units into one square. The xsize value indicates the extra size points that will fit in a square. Use a value of 2 for a normal formation fighting human.

fortkill.text: This monster will automatically destroy forts in the same province. Chance is the chance in percent that the fort will be destroyed each turn.

gcost.text: The cost in gold is also the cost in design points for pretenders. For shape changing pretenders, the gold cost should always be fixed. For other pretenders, the gcost can be set to 10000, meaning the cost will be calculated automatically based on attributes and special abilities. Pretender autocalc uses different rules than autocalc for normal units and commanders. To tweak the autocost add or subtract a small amount to the 10000 number.

gemprod.text: This monster produces a number of magic gems each month. The type ranges from 0 (fire gems) to 8 (blood slaves). See table "Magic path numbers".

giftofwater.text: A commander with this ability is able to bring a number of units underwater with him as long as their combined size points do not exceed the value of this ability.

glamour.text: Gives a monster the glamour ability of a Van (not the magic path with the same name). These monsters cannot be discovered by scouts and have a mirror image protecting them in battles. This command adds 25 to the monster's existing stealth value if it already has the #stealthy attribute. Glamour does not grant stealth to monsters that have no stealth to begin with.

glamourmanip.text: This monster is a glamour manipulator and counts as a glamour mage when it comes to upholding illusions and false damage. Monster Modding, New Abilities for Dominions 5 These Modding commands were new for Dominions 5 and have still not received any detailed descriptions.

glamourrange.text: Glamour magic cast by the monster have increased range.

godsite.text: The pretender will start with this site in its home province.

gold.text: The monster generates gold that is added to the treasury. Use a negative value for a monster that costs gold every month above and beyond the normal upkeep.

goodleader.text: Leadership value 100. Commanded units have a morale modifier of +1 for up to 3 squads and -1 for every additional squad.

goodmagicleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 100 magic beings. This is a very rare ability that only most magic beings possess.

goodundeadleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 100 undead beings. This is a rare ability that usually only demons or undead beings possess.

grandcom.text: This monster can participate in grand communions.

greaterhorror.text: Monsters with this tag are used as horrors. All horrors automatically gain spirit sight.

growhp.text: The monster grows into the previous monster once it has this many hit points or more. Hydras use this mechanic.

growthpower.text: The monster will get stat increases or decreases depending on the Growth scale.

guardspiritbonus.text: Increases the chance of receiving a guardian spirit with +value percent. Command has no effect if the nation does not have #guardspirit command set.

haltheretic.text: Works like Awe, except that it only works against sacred units.

heal.text: Grants Pangaea-like healing powers to the monster (Recuperation special ability).

healer.text: Grants a commander the Heal Troops ability. The percent value is the chance of success for every unit in the province. Success chance is checked against every unit to see if the commander successfully uses the healing ability. If successful, a check is made against the difficulty of each affliction and if it succeeds, the affliction in question is healed. Some afflictions are harder to heal than others. This command still works, but it is replaced in all instances of in-game occurrence with the #autohealer or #autodishealer mechanic.

heat.text: This monster is surrounded by heat like an Abysian. The heat aura is <value> + Fire magic squares in size. Standard value is 3.

heatrecscale.text: Heat scale requirement for recruitment. (The old #heatrec command also works, but is deprecated).

heretic.text: The monster decreases dominion in the province it resides in as if it was an enemy priest engaged in preaching. The value of the heretic ability acts as the priest level and should be set within the range of 1 – 5.

holy.text: Holy (sacred) troops can be blessed by priests.

holycost.text: Sets the holy point cost for recruiting this unit, minimum is 1. Can only be used on sacred units. If this command is not used they will cost the usual one holy point.

holyrange.text: Holy magic cast by the monster have increased range.

homerealm.text: Sets the home realm of the god, which makes the god available as a default choice for nations that belong to the same realm. See Table "Home realms" for home realm numbers. This command is not needed and should not be used if you only intend the god to be used by a single nation or a few nations instead of being widely available. Use #homerealm 0 to clear the homerealm of a pretender god.

homeshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when moving into its home province.

homesick.text: This monster takes damage equal to the indicated percentage of its total hit points every turn it spends away from its home province (the province where it was first recruited, summoned or spawned).

horrordeserter.text: Like #deserter, but the desertion chance is increased during astral corruption.

horrormark.text: Anyone striking this monster may be horror marked.

horsetattoo.text: Magic tattoo like the units of Marverni and Sauromatia have.

hp.text: The maximum number of hit points for the monster. A normal human has 10 hit points, a giant has 30 hit points and a huge dragon has 125 hit points.

hpoverflow.text: The monster's hit points can increase past the normal maximum. The extra HP are permanently retained until lost due to damage. This command is useful for units that possess life drain attacks or that can #digest swallowed monsters.

humanoid.text: The default bodytype. Use this for humans, ogres, angels, humanlike statues and similar.

iceforging.text: The monster generates <value> resources in cold provinces.

icenatprot.text: Natural protection varies with the temperature in the province. The protection value is added or subtracted for every step on the Cold scale.

iceprot.text: Armor protection varies with the temperature in the province. The protection value is added or subtracted for every step on the Cold scale.

illusion.text: This monster is an illusion. This is like spiritform, but illusions can be affected by illusion magic even if they are mindless and should otherwise be immune.

immobile.text: This monster is immobile and cannot move in combat. Immobile does not affect map move, use "#mapmove 0" to make a monster immobile on the strategic map.

immortal.text: This monster is immortal like a Lich.

inanimate.text: Inanimate beings are immune to some spells.

incorporate.text: The monster incorporates any swallowed creatures as a part of itself. Swallowed creatures take damage every combat round until dead or until the monster that swallowed them is killed. The monster that incorporates them heals a number of hit points equal to damage inflicted every combat round.

incprovdef.text: The monster is good at organizing province defenses. PD is increased by <value> per turn, to a maximum of 19.

incscale.text: Increases the selected scale by one point per turn to a maximum of -3 / 3. This command functions as #decscale for the opposite scales.

incunrest.text: The monster will increase or decrease unrest at his location. The value divided by 10 is the amount increased per month. A negative can be used to decrease unrest instead.

indepmove.text: This ability is used by certain horrors to make them move on the world map. A monster with this ability have percent chance of moving each month as long as it is owned by independents.

indepspells.text: Usually independent mages will only know low level research spells. This command will give them access to all spell with this research level and lower when they fight as independent.

indepstay.text: A 1 in this ability means that the monster will stop moving once it has reached a throne province.

infernoret.text: Extra chance per month of returning from the Inferno, the infernal realm of fire.

inquisitor.text: This monster has a bonus when preaching against enemy Dominion. Its holy magic level counts as double for this purpose. The monster must have the #holy tag.

insane.text: The monster has a chance of being insane each turn. The Mad Priests of R'lyeh have a value of 50 in this attribute.

insanify.text: The monster spreads insanity to both military units and population in the province. The percent value is the chance for a military unit in the same province to be infected.

inspirational.text: All units under the command of this monster have their morale increased by <bonus> in addition to modifiers from base leadership. Commander cost +10 per point. The value can be negative.

inspiringres.text: The monster inspires other mages to be more effective researchers. All other mages in the same province gain a research bonus equal to <value> while the monster stays in the province. Only the highest value present counts.

invisible.text: Invisible units can only be seen by units with spirit sight. When a unit with invisibility is sneaking, only patrolling units with spirit sight will be able to find it. In combat invisibility gives any melee attackers -10 to their attack skill unless they have spirit sight.

invulnerable.text: The monster has invulnerability to non-magical weapons. The invulnerability value counts as natural protection against normal weapons.

ironvul.text: The monster will take points amount of extra damage when wounded by an iron weapon in melee.

itemslots.text: Sets which item slots are available for this monster. See Table "Item slot values" for useful slot values. If you want to have 2 hand slots and 1 body slot then just add those two numbers together. Never add 1 hand and 1 hand, use the 2 hands value instead. The bottom three entries in the table are some precalculated values for your convenience. You can omit this command if you want the standard for the current bodytype (humanoid = 2 hands, 1 head, 1 body, 1 feet and 2 misc).

ivylord.text: This monster will receive extra units when summoning Vine Men of different kind.

kokytosret.text: Extra chance per month of returning from Kokytos, the infernal realm of ice.

labxpshape.text: The monster will change into the next monster type (next monster number) after reaching this amount of xp and when being in a province with a lab.

lamialord.text: This monster will receive extra units when summoning Lamias of different kind. This ability will not be visible when inspecting the monster.

lanceok.text: This monster can use lances even though it is not flying or mounted. Use this attribute on centaurs.

landdamage.text: The monster will take damage equal to the indicated percentage of its total hit points every turn it spends in a land province instead of underwater.

landshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when moving from a water province to a land province.

latehero.text: Use this command on a hero unit to prevent it from appearing before this turn.

leper.text: The monster spreads a very deadly disease that kills population and infects military units in the province. The percent value is the chance for a military unit in the same province to be infected.

lesserhorror.text: Monsters with this tag are used as lesser horrors. All horrors automatically gain spirit sight.

lich.text: The monster will get this shape if it is transformed into a lich.

lizard.text: Four legged beast, but lower. Use this for dragons.

localsun.text: This monster will count as the sun being present in the current province. This can be important when trying to cast certain spells that cannot be cast when there is no sun.

magicbeing.text: This monster is a magic being.

magicboost.text: Gives a boost or reduction to the monster's magic ability for one or all magic paths. The boost can be from -5 to 5 levels. See table "Magic path numbers" for path numbers (0-9, 51-53).

magiccommand.text: Increases magic leadership by this amount.

magicimmune.text: The monster is immune to the research effects of Drain and Magic scales. There is no research penalty for Drain scale and no research bonus for magic scale.

magicpower.text: The monster will get stat increases or decreases depending on the Magic scale.

magicskill.text: Gives a magic skill to the active monster. The path must be a number from the "Magic path numbers" table and level should be a number from 1 to 10. If the monster already has this magic skill then the old level will be replaced by the new one, unless it is a random skill. Units with Holy magic must also have the #holy command.

magicstudy.text: Research bonus depending on the magic scale of the province.

makemonsters1.text: Gives the monster a special order that can summon a monster per month. #makemonsters2 to #makemonsters5 can also be used to summon more monsters per month.

makepearls.text: The monster can turn <value> water gems to <value> astral pearls per turn.

mapmove.text: The speed at which the monster travels on the world map. The old Dominions 4 values are 1 for heavy infantry, 2 for a lightly armed human or knights and 3 for light cavalry. You can use these values and the game will automatically convert them to values suitable for Dominions 6. In Dominions 6 a human has mapmove 14 and a horse 20. A value of 0 will make the unit unable to move on the world map, except by means of teleport rituals. Armor will automatically reduce the map move and receiving a mount will increase it. See the following table for suitable mapmoves. Human | 14 Giant | 16 Vaetti | 12 Lizard | 12 Naga | 10 Wyrm | 14 Enkidu | 16 Satyr | 16 Legion | 18 Titan | 20 Caelum | 20 Zotz | 20 Abysia | 12 Atlantis | 12 Shambler | 14 Triton | 16 Bandar | 12 Vanara | 14 Colossi | 18 Pale One | 12 Ancient One | 14 Horse | 20 Feyhorse | 26 Serpent | 18 Undead | 20 Demon | 20

mapteleport.text: Like #teleport but only grants teleport ability on the map, not in combat.

mason.text: A mason is able to lead the construction of more advanced forts than what would otherwise be possible for the nation. A mason will be able to upgrade a fortress one step further than normally possible.

masterrit.text: Pathboost for the purpose of casting rituals. A monster with this ability can cast rituals that would require <value> higher magic paths than it actually has. A negative value makes the monster worse at casting rituals.

mastersmith.text: The monster's magic paths are counted as <value> higher than actual when forging items so a mage with a bonus of 1 and Fire magic 1 would be able to forge items that require Fire 2 to forge. A negative value makes the monster worse at forging items.

maxage.text: This maximum age for a monster. After this age it will risk getting afflictions and eventually die. Default is 50 for humans, 500 for undead, 1000 for demons. Different magic paths increase maxage 50% of this value per point of magic, depending on the type of creature. Undead are affected by Death magic, inanimate creatures by Earth magic, demons by Blood magic and all others by Nature magic, in that order (if the monster belongs to more than one of these categories at once, e.g. lifeless undead).

maxdeadhp.text: The monster's bonus HP gained from corpse eating can never go above this.

maxprison.text: Sets the maximum imprisonment level for this pretender. 0=disabled, 1=awake, 2=dormant. Note that the numbers mean different things than in #minprison.

mindcollar.text: Unit will take this amount of damage if it breaks in combat.

mindvessel.text: Monster can be the target of the mind vessel ritual.

minprison.text: Sets the minimum imprisonment level for this pretender. 0=awake, 1=dormant, 2=imprisoned. The Uttervast pretender god has this attribute.

minsizeleader.text: Selects the nametype that will be affected by the following modding commands. Nametype nbr is a number between 100 and 399. See Table Name Types below. Numbers 170 – 399 can be used to make your own name tables without altering existing ones.

miscshape.text: Use this for strange things like cubes or fountains.

mobilearcher.text: Mobile archers can shoot while their mount is moving. This is used for mobile archer cavalry units.

monpresentrec.text: This monster can only be recruited if a unit of "monster name" type is present in the recruiting province. Montag numbers can be used.

montag.text: This command assigns a monster tag value to a creature. The value must be a number between 1000 and 100000. The monster tag value is a summoning marker that can be used with the other monster summoning commands and in spell modding to summon randomly determined monsters from a defined list. When a summoning command or spell is used with the montag value, a random creature with that montag value is summoned. Use a minus sign before the value when using it in this manner for the command to work correctly. Example: Five monsters with a #montag 2500 could be set as random monster summons by assigning #summon2 -2500 to another monster. This would result in two random monsters from those five being summoned. The monster tag can also be used as damage value for summoning spells, which will then summon a random monster from the group with the same tag. To use it that way, set spell damage to (minus)<montag value>.

montagweight.text: Use this command after a montag command to make it more likely to appear than other monster with the same montag. The weight defaults to 1 which gives this montag the same chance of occurring as other montags with weight 1 (or no specified weight). A weight of 2 will make it twice as likely to appear, and so forth. Maximum weight is 100.

mor.text: The morale of the monster. A normal human soldier has morale 10, a satyr of Pangaea has 8 and a fierce minotaur has 13. Giving a monster 50 in morale makes it mindless and prone to dissolving due to lack of proper leadership. Undead with a mind but nothing to lose usually have 30 in morale.

moregrowth.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreheat.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreluck.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moremagic.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreorder.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreprod.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

mountainsurvival.text: Monster has the Mountain Survival skill. Mountain terrain does not hinder movement and the monster can cross mountain passes even if it is cold in the provinces the pass connects.

mounted.text: This command should only be used in rare cases where the Dominions 6 system of seperate stats for rider and mount is not suitable. It was used for mounted units in Dominions 5 where the rider and horse shared the same stats. This command will give a defence bonus to the unit as well as reduced encumbrance.

mountedhumanoid.text: Regarding hit locations this is the same as humanoid, but it removes the boot item slot and is provided for convenience for centaurs and similar. Don't use it for knight, they should be humanoid and then mounted on a horse that is an quadruped.

mountiscom.text: If this is set to one the mount is also a commander. This command is used for some gods that has divine mounts.

mountmnr.text: Use this to give a mount to a rider. The sprite of the unit should be the standard sprite of the rider sitting on his mount.

mr.text: The magic resistance of the monster. A normal human has 10, 1st level mages have 13 and 3rd level mages have 15. No one has magic resistance above 18, except some beings from the void that may have up to 20.

naga.text: Snake like lower part and a humanoid upper body. Use this for nagas.

name.text: This must be the first command for every new monster. It sets the name of the monster.

nametype.text: Sets the type of random name that this monster gets when it’s a commander. For name numbers and their meaning see table "Name Types".

naturerange.text: Nature magic cast by the monster have increased range.

neednoteat.text: This monster doesn’t need any food and doesn’t consume any supplies. To create a monster that cannot starve but still eats, combine this effect with a negative #supplybonus.

newmonster.text: Monster nbr should be a number between 5000 and 8999. It must not be the same as any other monster. This new monster will be affected by the following modding commands and there should be an #end command at the end. It is not necessary to set a monster number when creating a new monster. It is not recommended to use a monster number with monsters that have unique names like Sorceress of the Sacred Fire because that will reduce the risk of conflicts between mods. If a monster number is not used, Dominions will automatically use the first free number from 5000+ for the monster. In this instance all references to the monster in other modding (such as spells or magic sites) must be by name. Using lower hard coded numbers later in the mod may overwrite the number initially assigned by a numberless #newmonster command.

nightmareaura.text: Grant the Nightmare Aura effect with this area of effect.

nobadevents.text: The monster will reduce the chance of negative events in his current province. The value is the percent chance of negating a possible bad event.

nobarding.text: This mount does not have a barding slot. This is used for e.g. the humans that carry a throne with an emperor in it.

nofalldmg.text: This rider will not take any damage when falling off his mount. This is used for chariot drivers that are always close to the ground.

nofmounts.text: Sets the number of mounts that this rider has. The default is one and usually there is no need for this command. But e.g. an emperor with two people carrying his throne needs two mounts.

nofriders.text: Sets the number of riders that sits on the same mount. The default is one and usually there is no need for this command. But e.g. a elephant rider that is accomanied by two more people on top of the elephant would need this command with a value of 3.

noheal.text: This monster does not heal naturally. If it is a magic being it will heal if it is located in a province with a lab.

nohof.text: The monster cannot enter the Hall of Fame.

noitem.text: This monster can only use misc items.

noleader.text: This monster cannot lead units when it is a commander. Use this for scouts and assassins.

nomagicleader.text: This monster cannot lead magic units when it is a commander (unless it it is a mage). This is the default.

nomovepen.text: Monster ignores movement penalty from armor. This is used for chariots.

norange.text: The chance in percent that the unit will skip standing still and fire. Horrors with range weapons have this ability.

noremount.text: The commander will no be able to reclaim his mount through a reclaim mount order. This is used for certain gods that have divine mounts that must be prayed back.

noreqlab.text: Recruiting this monster never requires a lab, even if it is a mage.

noreqtemple.text: Recruiting the monster never requires a temple, even if it is sacred.

noriverpass.text: The monster is unable to cross rivers even when they are frozen, like a vampire.

notdomshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when not inside a friendly dominion.

nothrowoff.text: This mount will not throw off its rider if it routs or gets paralyzed. This is used on mounts that are more important than the rider, e.g. elephants, where the rider will never get off voluntarily in order to fight on the ground.

noundeadleader.text: This monster cannot lead undead units when it is a commander (unless it it is a death or blood mage). This is the default.

noweapon.text: Use this on monsters with no weapons that are not supposed to attack at all in combat. This will prevent them from getting a fist or a headbutt as default weapon. Immobile units do not need this command.
values: Head slots can only have crowns
2 hands, bow, head (crown), body, feet, 2 misc

nowish.text: This monster cannot be wished for.

okleader.text: Leadership value 50. This is the default value and it is the standard for non-elite commanders. Commanded units have a morale modifier of 0 for two or fewer squads and -1 for every additional squad.

okmagicleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 50 magic beings. This is a very rare ability that only most magic beings possess.

okundeadleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 50 undead beings. This is a rare ability that usually only demons or undead beings possess.

older.text: Makes the monster start somewhat older or younger than its calculated or preset start age.

onebattlespell.text: Monster will automatically cast this spell just before the battle starts. There is no fatigue cost. This spell cannot be a spell added by a mod, it must be an original Dominions 6 spell. You can modify the spell used by this command though. This ability only works for commanders.

onisummon.text: This unit has a chance of attracting one or more Ko-Oni per month. The Oni will only come if there is unrest or a turmoil scale in the province. The higher the unrest and turmoil the greater chance that a group of Ko-Oni will appear. The value of this ability will also modify this chance. A normal value is 50.

overcharged.text: Grants the overcharged ability. A damage value of 1 means that it is a capped damage, greater values give uncapped damage.

ownsmonrec.text: This monster can only be recruited if a unit of "monster name" type is owned by the recruiting player. Montag numbers can be used.

pathcost.text: The cost for a new path in design points when this monster is used as a god. Standard is a value between 10 (arch mage) and 80 (dragon). By using this command the monster will also be selectable as a god.

patience.text: The patience value increases the chances of the assassin to catch his target unawares and without bodyguards. Each point of patience decreases the chance of bodyguards being present by 10%. If the bodyguard unit has the Bodyguard ability, it reduces the effectiveness of the assassin's Patience.

patrolbonus.text: A value of ten will make this monster count as ten extra humans when it comes to patrolling. This value can also be negative for extra poor performance.

pierceres.text: The monster takes half damage from piercing weapons.

pillagebonus.text: A monster with this ability excels at pillaging. A barbarian has a pillage bonus of one which makes them count as one man extra when it comes to pillaging.

plaguedoctor.text: A commander with this ability can use the make plague order.

plainshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when moving from a forest province to a non-forest province. If the monster also has a watershape, the watershape takes precedence over the plainshape, such as when moving from a forest to a water province.

plant.text: The monster is a plant. Plants cannot be turned into zombies by Raise Dead or other methods.

poisonarmor.text: Anyone striking this monster with short weapons will be poisoned.

poisoncloud.text: Monster is surrounded by a poison cloud. Standard size is 6.

poisonres.text: Grants poison resistance to the monster.

poisonskin.text: The monster has a skin that exudes a paralyzing poison, which does fatigue damage to anyone attacking it with length 0 weapons. The value is the damage rating of the poison.

polyimmune.text: This monster cannot be polymorphed and it cannot transform itself using rituals either.

pooramphibian.text: This monster can travel under water, but is hindered by it.

poorleader.text: Leadership value 10. This is the standard value for mages. Commanded units have a morale modifier of -1 if in a single squad and an additional -1 for every additional squad.

poormagicleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 10 magic beings. This is a very rare ability that only most magic beings possess.

poorundeadleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 10 undead beings. This is a rare ability that usually only demons or undead beings possess.

popkill.text: The monster kills (10 x amount) of population in the province it resides in every month. This applies to both commander and non-commander units with this attribute.

powerofdeath.text: The monster will become more powerful every time it dies, up to at most limit number of deaths.

praise.text: The praise ability raises friendly dominion in the province.

prec.text: The basic precision of the monster. A normal human archer has 10.

prophetshape.text: Unit will change into this monster when made a prophet. Monster nbr can be negative for montag usage.

prot.text: The monster’s natural protection. This value should be 0 for all humans, 5 for a lizardman or about 18 for a huge and scaly dragon.

quadruped.text: Four legged beasts. Use this for Elephants, lions, wolves and similar.

raiseonkill.text: Monster has a chance in percent to raise the people it kills as soulless.

raiseshape.text: Changes soulless to another kind of unit for the #raiseonkill or #dt_raise effects. Monster number can be negative for montag usage.

randomspell.text: The monster has a <percent> chance of casting a random spell in combat instead of a good one. The ability only works for commanders, because only commanders can cast spells.

raredomsummon.text: There is a flat 8% chance of summoning one creature of this type when in a province with friendly dominion.

rcost.text: The cost in resources. The resource cost of weapons and armor will be added to this. Most human troops have a rcost of one.

reanimator.text: The monster will reanimate this number of corpses automatically every turn.

reanimpriest.text: A priest with this attribute will be able to raise undead.

reclimit.text: The monster can only be recruited in limited numbers. You can only recruit <units / turn> of this monster in any one province. 0 and lower values have special meanings: 0 = no reclimit, -1 = 0/turn, -2 = -1/turn.

reconst.text: Works like regeneration, but only affects inanimate beings.

reform.text: This is a combat ability. The monster has this chance of getting a new healthy body when killed.

reformtime.text: Alters the time taken to reform the immortal's body. The standard time is 3 months, use #reformtime -2 if you want the immortal to reappear the next month.

regainmount.text: If this is set to one the rider will regain any lost mount(s) for free after the battle. This only works for commanders.

regeneration.text: The monster regenerates like a troll and heals damage every combat round. The percent value indicates how many percent of its total hit points are regenerated every turn. The standard value for regeneration is 10.

reinvigoration.text: Reduces the fatigue by points amount every turn in battle. This value can be negative to gain extra fatigue in battle instead. Lower fatigue reduces the chance of the monster suffering critical hits while higher fatigue increases it.

reqlab.text: Recruiting the monster requires a lab.

reqtemple.text: Recruiting the monster requires a temple.

researchbonus.text: Makes a commander better or worse at magic research. A sage has a value of 8.

resources.text: The monster generates <value> resources in the province it is in, like a Master Smith of Ulm.

ressize.text: Use this command with a size value of 3 to give a flier resource cost calculated based on size 3 instead of 4. Size value must be a number between 1 and 10.

rpcost.text: The cost in recruitment points for the monster. 1 is standard for a simple commander and about 10 for a normal soldier. A value of "base price"*1000 means it will be auto- calculated. Most human troops and commander have the value 10000, meaning that it will be calculated automatically based on the monster's age and that it has a base price of 10 gold, commanders also have magic and other skills taken into account.

sabbathslave.text: The monster is automatically a sabbath slave and does not need to cast the Communion Slave spell to join a sabbath.

sailing.text: A commander with this ability is able to sail over two sea provinces with his troops. Ship size is the size of the boat and indicates how many size points the commander can transport. Standard value is 999. Max unit size is the maximum size unit that can be transported, usually 3 or 5.

scalewalls.text: The monster can assassinate commanders even when they are in besieged castles.

secondshape.text: This monster will assume another shape when it gets seriously wounded. Remember to give the other shape the #firstshape command if you want it to return to the primary form when it feels better. Werewolves in human form use this ability. Monster nbr can be negative for montags.

secondtmpshape.text: This monster will transform into another monster when it is killed in battle. This other monster will be removed after battle. Serpent Cataphracts use this ability. Monster nbr can be negative for montags.

seduce.text: Gives the monster the ability to seduce like a Nagini. The value indicates the difficulty of the morale check, 10 is standard.

selectmonster.text: Selects the monster that will be affected by the following modding commands. End modding this unit with the #end command. To find out what number a particular unit has, look at his stats in the game and press ctrl+i.

shapechance.text: Extra chance of the shapechange or secondshape transformations actually taking effect. Default chance is 100, so this chance should be negative to have any effect. E.g. a monster with shapechance -75 would only have a 25% chance of getting to his second shape when the first one gets killes.

shapechange.text: This monster is able to change shape to and from another monster at will. The other monster is not affected by this command and must be given #shapechange command with the first form as the value. Dragons use this ability. It is also possible to do multiple form shape changers such as the Jotun Skratti by chaining this command over several monsters.

shatteredsoul.text: The monster suffers from a shattered soul like a Tartarian. There is a <percent> chance each turn that the monster (if a commander) does not obey orders but does something else instead.

shockres.text: Grants shock resistance to the monster.

shrinkhp.text: The monster shrinks to the following monster once it has this many hit points or less. Hydras use this mechanic.

siegebonus.text: A value of ten will make this monster count as ten extra humans when it comes to breaking down castle gates.

singlebattle.text: The monster only fights in one battle and then leaves, like the gladiators of Ermor and Pythium. It has to kill someone or get wounded to count as having fought.

size.text: The size of the monster. 1 = bug, 2 = hoburg, 3 = human & wolf, 4 = bandar & lion, 5 = enkidu & horse, 6 = jotun giant & ice drake, 7 = anakite & cave grub, 8 = small titan & monster boar, 9 = large titan & elephant, 10 = dragon. Monsters with wings usually get 1 extra size, e.g. a flying human sized unit should have size 4.

skilledrider.text: A skilled rider will increase the Morale and Defence Skill of his mount. The defence increase is most effective on lightly armored horses as it is reduced by the encumbrance value of the mount's armor. This ability should be given to the rider and not to the mount.

skirmisher.text: Selects the nametype that will be affected by the following modding commands. Nametype nbr is a number between 100 and 399. See Table Name Types below. Numbers 170 – 399 can be used to make your own name tables without altering existing ones.

slashres.text: The monster takes half damage from slashing weapons.

slave.text: Slaves are typically untrained fodder who are given weapons and herded into battle. They have low morale and are easily routed. Their morale is improved when led by a taskmaster.

slaver.text: Gets the capture slave ability. The number of slaves captured will be 1d6+4 (open ended) per month and unrest will increase by 1 for every slave captured.

slaverbonus.text: Modifies the number of slaves captured with the Slaver ability. E.g. a modifier of -2 will make the slaver ability catch 1d6+2 slaves per month.

sleepaura.text: Grant the Sleep Aura effect with this area of effect. The Shuten-doji has this ability with area 10.

sleepres.text: Monster will get the Undreaming ability giving this bonus to its MR against sleep effects.

slimer.text: Any unit attacking this monster must make a magic resistance check or become immobilized by oozing slime, identical to the effects of the Slime spell. Strength works identically to #damagerev.

slothpower.text: The monster will get stat increases or decreases depending on the Sloth scale.

slothresearch.text: The monster gains <value> research bonus per step of sloth in the province.

slowrec.text: Takes double the amount of commander points to recruit this monster, it can only be used on commanders.

smartmount.text: The smartness determines the chance for the mount to try to make it home. A smart magical unicorn has smartness 100, a normal horse doesn't have this ability at all.

snake.text: Use this for snakes, wyrms and other monsters without legs.

snaketattoo.text: Magic tattoo like the units of Marverni and Sauromatia have.

snow.text: The monster is unhindered by snow.

sorcerygems.text: This monster produces a number of magic gems each month. They are of a single random type of sorcery gem.

sorceryrange.text: Sorcery (Astral, Death, Nature, Glamour) rituals by the monster have increased range.

speciallook.text: This command surround a monster with a particle effect. Value can be from 1 to 3 and represents fire shield look, astral shield look and a burning look respectively. A value of 100 to 199 will give the unit a fixed alpha value of 0-99 (low values will make it impossible to see).

spellsinger.text: Unit takes 50% longer to cast spells, but at half fatigue cost.

spikes.text: This unit is covered in sharp spikes barbs. Anyone striking it with a short weapon (length no more than 1) will risk getting damaged. The damage is not severe, it is capped at 1 point and armor also protects.

spiritform.text: This monster is a spiritlike being and is immune to certain spells like stoneskin and polymorph.

spiritsight.text: Spirit sight makes it possible to see into the spirit realm and see the true essence of beings. Units with spirit sight gets no penalties from darkness and can see invisible units.

spr1.text: The file name of the normal image for the monster. The size of the image should be 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128 pixels wide/high. A human being should be about 32 pixels high and there should be 2 pixels of free space between his feet and the bottom of the image. You can use an alpha channel in the image or not. If not you should instead use black (RGB 0 0 0) as background and magenta (RGB 255 0 255) for shadows.

spr2.text: The file name of the attack image for the monster. If this is not set, then spr1 will be used for this image too.

spreaddom.text: The monster spreads the Dominion of the pretender god by its mere presence. The candles value should usually be one, meaning that the monster spreads as much dominion as one prophet.

springimmortal.text: The immortal will reform his body in the spring.

springpower.text: The monster has increased hit points in spring and lowered hit points in autumn.

springshape.text: Changes into another monster when this season is active.

standard.text: The monster increases the morale of units in the same squad by <bonus>. Multiple standards in the same squad do not stack. Only the highest standard value in the squad counts. The normal value for this command is 1.

startaff.text: The monster has a chance of starting with a random lesser affliction like a flagellant.

startage.text: The start age for a monster. Usually there is no need to set this as it will be calculated automatically depending on maxage and skills. An age of zero clears this command and an age of -1 sets start age to zero. The startage value is the starting point for actual age calculations based on magic and other skills.

startdom.text: The default dominion strength this monster is used as a god. Standard is a value between 1 (arch mage) and 4 (oracle). This command also makes the monster selectable as a god.

startheroab.text: The monster has a chance of starting with a heroic ability, like you receive when entering the hall of fame.

startingaff.text: Monster always starts with one (or more) afflictions as indicated by the affliction bitmask. See the Affliction table in the weapon modding section for suitable values.

startitem.text: The monster starts with this item if it is a commander. This command can be used multiple times on the same monster for more than 1 starting weapon.

startmajoraff.text: The monster has a chance of starting with a random major affliction.

statbreak.text: 1+ = Can break siege even if it is stationary (map move 0), which would otherwise make it unable to.

statstorm.text: 1+ = Can storm forts even if it is stationary (map move 0), which would otherwise make it unable to.

stealthy.text: This monster can sneak into enemy provinces. The default value when using this modding command is 0. Scouts are harder to detect and have a standard value of 10. A Spy has 20. The number of patrolling units required to have a 50% chance of detecting the sneaking monster is <value> + 40. This means that 40 patrolling units are required to have a 50% chance of detecting a standard stealthy unit, while 50 patrolling units are required to have an equal chance of detecting a sneaking scout.

stonebeing.text: This monster is a stone being and immune to petrification.

stormimmune.text: This monster can fly during a storm. If the monster has the #stormpower attribute, this command is redundant.

stormpower.text: The monster gets stat increases in combat during storms. This attribute also duplicates the effects of the #stormimmune attribute, giving the monster the ability to fly during a storm. Only active in combat.

str.text: The strength of the monster. A normal human soldier has 10, a giant has 20 and a dragon has 25 or more.

succubus.text: Gives the monster the dream seduction ability like a Succubus. The value indicates the difficulty of the morale check, 10 is standard.

summerpower.text: The monster has increased hit points in summer and lowered hit points in winter.

summershape.text: Changes into another monster when this season is active.

summon1.text: Automatically summons monsters each month. The #summon1 command summons one monster per month and #summon2 to #summon5 more according to the number in the command.

sunawe.text: Works like Awe, except that it doesn't work if there is no sun shining.

superiorleader.text: Leadership value 200. Commanded units have a morale modifier of +3.

superiormagicleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 200 magic beings. This is a very rare ability that only most magic beings possess.

superiorundeadleader.text: This monster has an innate ability to command 200 undead beings. This is a rare ability that usually only demons or undead beings possess.

supplybonus.text: A monster with this ability produces extra supplies.

swampsurvival.text: Monster has the Swamp Survival skill. Swamp terrain does not hinder movement.

tainted.text: Chance in percent of being horror marked each turn.

taskmaster.text: All slaves under the command of this monster have their morale increased by <bonus>.

taxcollector.text: The monster can collect taxes from provinces that cannot trace a route to the nearest fort.

teleport.text: The monster can teleport. Movement on the battlefield is instantaneous and the monster is not hindered by storms. The command automatically sets mapmove to 100 and the creature ignores terrain restrictions and the Sea of Ice spell.

templetrainer.text: A commander with this ability will be able to summon a monster per turn when in a temple province. Only one commander can do this per temple province.

thronekill.text: This monster will automatically destroy thrones in the same province, unless they are protected by a fort. Chance is the chance in percent that the throne will be destroyed each turn.

tmpairgems.text: The monster produces a number of air gems that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tmpastralgems.text: The monster produces a number of astral pearls that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tmpbloodslaves.text: The monster can use his own blood equal to this number of blood slaves for combat spell casting. Using a temporary blood slave this way will result in the profuse bleeding affliction on the caster.

tmpdeathgems.text: The monster produces a number of death gems that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tmpearthgems.text: The monster produces a number of earth gems that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tmpfiregems.text: The monster produces a number of fire gems that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tmpglamourgems.text: The monster produces a number of glamour gems that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tmpnaturegems.text: The monster produces a number of nature gems that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tmpwatergems.text: The monster produces a number of water gems that can be used in combat. The gems are not stable enough to be used for ritual spellcasting.

tolerateund.text: Will tolerate undead beings in same squad without receiving any morale penalty. This command is used for the units in the squad, not the leader.

trample.text: This monster can trample smaller beings.

trampswallow.text: The monster automatically swallows the targets of a successful trampling attack. Swallowed monsters are removed from the battlefield until the swallowing monster is killed.

transformation.text: The monster is a possible target for the Transformation spell. Value can be -1 for a bad result, 0 to disable and 1 for a good result. #(path)attuned <chance> Chance of getting a bonus level of magic when transformed into this being. In place of (path), insert the name of the magic path in all lower case for the correct command (#fireattuned, #airattuned etc).

triple3mon.text: The trinity god has 3 different monsters. The monsters must be created after one another and the first one should be used as the god. Only the first monster needs this command.

triplegod.text: The pretender is a Trinity God. Splits god into three when game starts. The type value determines how the magic should be split between the 3 pretenders. Type: 1=full magic, 2=split magic, 3=reduced magic, 4=like the grey one, 5=like titan of the crossroads.

triplegodmag.text: Magic penalty for trinity gods when they are not in the same province. The penalty is usually set to 2.

troglodyte.text: Use this for humanoids without a head.

truesight.text: True sight makes it possible to see through illusions and glamour. Units with true sight get no penalties when fighting units who are invisible or enchanted with glamour spells such as Blur.

twiceborn.text: The monster will get this shape if it dies and rises again due to the twiceborn ritual.

twistfate.text: Will start with a twist fate in combat. Also receives a twist fate at the start of each new month.

undcommand.text: Increases undead leadership by this amount.

undisciplined.text: Undisciplined monsters cannot be given orders in battle. They can only deploy in the skirmish formation and will attack the enemy without regard for any battle plan.

undregen.text: Works like regeneration, but only affects undead beings.

unify.text: Any one of the trinity gods can use the unify order to call the other parts of the trinity.

unique.text: There can only be one of this monster. If it dies and is resummoned, it will still be the same monster and it will have retained experience, curses, afflictions, magic etc.

unmountedspr1.text: Creates a sprite that is used when the rider loses his mount.

unmountedspr2.text: The attack animation sprite for the unmounted sprite. This must always be set after unmountedspr1 has been set, not before. Special units can have multiple mounts with the same rider, or many riders on the same mount. It is not possile to have multiple riders and multiple mounts at once though.

unseen.text: Like invisible, but will pop once hit.

unsurr.text: Selects the nametype that will be affected by the following modding commands. Nametype nbr is a number between 100 and 399. See Table Name Types below. Numbers 170 – 399 can be used to make your own name tables without altering existing ones.

unteleportable.text: The monster cannot use Teleport, Gateway or Astral Travel spells to move. It can still use Stygian Paths and Faery Trod.

userestricteditem.text: The monster can use restricted items of the same value. Value can be 1-10000. See Item Modding for more information.

uwbug.text: Monsters with this tag are summoned by the Swarm spell underwater.

uwdamage.text: This monster takes damage equal to the indicated percentage of its total hit points every turn it spends underwater (i.e. in a sea province). Vampires have #uwdamage 100 so they cannot go underwater at all.

uwfireshield.text: Like fireshield, but works underwater too.

uwregen.text: Works like regeneration, but only works underwater.

voidret.text: Extra chance per month of returning from the Void, the plane between worlds and the home of horrors and the Void beings of R'lyeh.

voidsanity.text: Reduces susceptibility to insanity. Insanity chance is divided by <value>, e.g. 10. Horrors and Void beings have a voidsanity value of 20.

warning.text: This ability lets a commander avoid assassination and seduction attempts.

wastesurvival.text: Monster has the Waste Survival skill. Waste terrain does not hinder movement.

waterelementals.text: Gives a size bonus to summoned water elementals.

waterrange.text: Water magic cast by the monster have increased range.

watershape.text: The monster changes to this shape when moving from a land province to a water province.

weapon.text: Equips the monster with this weapon. A monster can have multiple weapons and all melee weapons will be used simultaneously. All weapons found in Dominions can be used, but some different weapons have the same name so you might have to use the weapon number instead. The most common weapons can be found among the weapon tables. Press ctrl+i when viewing a unit’s stats to find out the weapon, armor and monster number for that particular unit. When modding an existing monster that already has weapons, each new #weapon command will add a new weapon to the monster. If you want to change the monster’s weapons without adding new ones, you must use the #clearweapons command to remove the existing weapons first.

winterpower.text: The monster has increased hit points in winter and lowered hit points in summer.

wintershape.text: Changes into another monster when this season is active.

wolftattoo.text: Magic tattoo like the units of Marverni and Sauromatia have.

worldshape.text: The monster changes to this shape when not in battle.

woundfend.text: The monster is less likely to suffer an affliction when taking damage. A value of 1 makes it half as likely, a value of 2 makes it one third as likely, etc. Air Elementals and similar have a value of 99, making it almost impossible to get an affliction.

xpgain.text: Will earn XP this many percent faster (or slower) than normal units.

xploss.text: The monster loses 0-100% of xp when changing shape due to taking damage.

xpshape.text: The monster will change into the next monster type (next monster number) after reaching this amount of xp.

xpshapeloss.text: The monster loses 0-100% of xp when changing shape due xpshape/xplabshape.

xpshapemon.text: Alters what monster xpshape & labxpshape transforms into. Monster number can be negative for montag usage.

xspr1.text: Creates a sprite that is used when one corider is lost. This command must be placed right after the #spr1 and #spr2 commands. If a there are more than 1 corider the #xspr1 and #xspr2 commands can be repeated multiple times to create sprites with fewer and fewer riders left.

xspr2.text: Creates the attack sprite that is used when one corider is lost. This command must be place right after the #xspr1 command.

yearturn.text: Power of the Turning Year. This unit is more powerful during the height of each season and will get increased Strength, Attack and Defence during those months.

addname.text: Adds a name to the selected nametype. A single nametype can contain up to 1499 different names.

clear.text: Removes all names from the selected nametype. 170-399 Custom name lists

end.text: Always use this command at the end of modifying a nametype.

selectnametype.text: Selects the nametype that will be affected by the following modding commands. Nametype nbr is a number between 100 and 399. See Table Name Types below. Numbers 170 – 399 can be used to make your own name tables without altering existing ones.

addforeigncom.text: This commander can only be recruited in provinces with no fort. #(terrain)rec "<monster name>" | <monster nbr> This unit can be recruited in (terrain) provinces without a fort. See the box below for all possible terrain names. So a complete command would be e.g. #forestrec "Moose". Combine this command with the next one (...fortrec) to create a unit that is recruitable in a specific terrain regardless of the presence of a fort. Note that "foreign" can only be used with the fortrec command. #(terrain)fortrec "<monster name>" | <monster nbr> This unit can be recruited in (terrain) provinces with a fort. See the box below for all terrain names. Note that sea, deep and kelp have no fortrec variants, use #uwrec and #uwcom instead. plain forest mountain (highlands and mountains) swamp waste farm cave (all type of caves) drip (drip caves) coast sea (shallow seas) deep (deep seas) kelp (kelp seas) foreign (non-capital forts)

addforeignunit.text: This unit can only be recruited in provinces with no fort.

addgod.text: Adds this monster as a god to the nation's list of valid gods. The monster must have the #startdom and #pathcost commands set. If the monster does not have a defined homerealm, this command is the only way to add it as a god.

addreccom.text: Add a unit to the list of recruitable commanders for this nation.

addrecunit.text: Add a unit to the list of recruits for this nation.

aiairnation.text: Hint to AI that Air magic is used a lot in this nation and that an air god is probably good.

aiastralnation.text: Hint to AI that Astral magic is used a lot in this nation and that an astral god is probably good.

aiawake.text: When playing this nation, the AI will have this much extra chance of choosing an awake pretender.

aibloodnation.text: Hint to AI that Blood magic is used a lot in this nation and that a blood god is probably good.

aicheapholy.text: Informs the AI that this nation has cheap expendable sacred units. So a Charge Body bless effect or something similar could be appropriate. Marignon and Mictlan has this hint.

aideathnation.text: Hint to AI that Death magic is used a lot in this nation and that a death god is probably good.

aiearthnation.text: Hint to AI that Earth magic is used a lot in this nation and that a earth god is probably good.

aifirenation.text: Hint to AI that Fire magic is used a lot in this nation and that a fire god is probably good.

aiglamournation.text: Hint to AI that Glamour magic is used a lot in this nation and that a glamour god is probably good.

aigoodbless.text: Use to increase the chance of creating a powerful bless. 100=only do gods with a powerful bless effects for this nation.

aiheavyrec.text: Will make the AI more likely to recruit troops that cost 15 or more resources. The number is the chance for the AI reconsider a non-heavy troop recruitment.

aiholdgod.text: When playing this nation, the AI will never leave the home province with the pretender.

aiholyranged.text: Informs the AI that this nation has sacred ranged units. So a Wind Guide bless or something similar could be appropriate.

aimagerec.text: Will make the AI more likely to recruit mage commanders than other commanders. The number is the chance for the AI reconsider a non-mage commander recruitment.

aimusthavemag.text: Makes AI pretender have at least 3 in this magic school. Only one of these possible per nation.

ainaturenation.text: Hint to AI that Nature magic is used a lot in this nation and that a nature god is probably good.

airblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

aiwaternation.text: Hint to AI that Water magic is used a lot in this nation and that a water god is probably good.

astralblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

autoundead.text: The nation's Dominion automatically spawns undead like Ashen Empire Ermor.

badindpd.text: This nation will not have national PD troops in any forted province except the home province.

blessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points.

bloodblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

bloodnation.text: Makes the AI more likely to research blood magic and hunt for blood slaves. Mictlan has this hint.

brief.text: A very brief description for popups.

buildcoastfort.text: The nation will build this type of fort in coastal provinces instead of the default one for their fortera.

buildfort.text: The nation will build this type of fort instead of the default one for their fortera.

builduwfort.text: The nation will build this type of underwater fort instead of the default one for their fortera.

castleprod.text: Resource bonus for forts. Middle Era Ulm has 25 in this, meaning they get 25% more resources in their fortified provinces than another nation with the same fort. Default is 0.

caveinc.text: Bonus in percent to income for all cave forts. Cave nations usually have about 15 in this value, other nations usually have 0 (the default).

cavelabcost.text: Gold cost for building a lab in a cave. Default is 600.

cavenation.text: Sets the nation's preference for starting in cave provinces. 0 = never start in caves, 1 = can start in caves, 2 = always start in a cave, 3 = start directly under a cave entrance

caverecpt.text: Bonus in percent to recruitment points (for units) for all cave forts.

caveres.text: Bonus in percent to resources for all cave forts.

cavetemplecost.text: Gold cost for building a temple in a cave. Default is 600.

cheapgod20.text: Nation can choose this god for 20 design points less.

cheapgod40.text: Nation can choose this god for 40 design points less.

cleargods.text: Clears the list of pretender gods for this nation. The #clearnation command also does this. This command does not clear homerealm, but #clearnation does. Homerealm gods must be removed with the #delgod command.

clearnation.text: Clears away all special settings for the nation, like ideal cold, reanimating priests, underwater nation, starting sites, heroes, pretender god list, local defense, fort type, etc. The list of recruitable units and commanders is not cleared with this command.

clearrec.text: Clears the list of recruitable units and commanders (but not gods) for this nation.

clearsites.text: Clears all start sites for this nation.

coastcom1.text: This command is deprecated and should not be used.

coastnation.text: The nation's capital is in a coastal land province.

coastunit1.text: This command is deprecated and should not be used.

color.text: Each of the three colors is a number between 0.0 and 1.0. This color is used for the score graphs.

deathblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

defchaos.text: Sets the default value of the chaos scale for this nation.

defcom1.text: Commander for local defense. This command also removes all old defense settings and must be used when changing the defense composition.

defcom2.text: Extra commander for fortified provinces with a province defense equal to or greater than 20.

defdeath.text: Sets the default value of the death scale for this nation.

defdrain.text: Sets the default value of the drain scale for this nation.

defmisfortune.text: Sets the default value of the misfortune scale for this nation.

defmult1.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense. E.g. #defmult1 20 will yield 2 units per point of defense, which is also the default.

defmult1b.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense for the second unit type. The default value is 10.

defmult1c.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense for the third unit type. The default value is 10.

defmult1d.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense for the fourth unit type. The default value is 10.

defmult2.text: Number of bonus units per 10 points of defense equal to or greater than 20.

defmult2b.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense equal to or greater than 20 for the second bonus unit type. The default value is 10.

defsloth.text: Sets the default value of the sloth scale for this nation.

defunit1.text: Standard unit for local defense in provinces with forts. Without forts, they appear at PD 20+.

defunit1b.text: Second type of standard unit for local defense. They appear like defunit1.

defunit1c.text: Third type of standard unit for local defense. They appear like defunit1. Usually there is no third type and this command isn't used.

defunit1d.text: Fourth type of standard unit for local defense. They appear like defunit1. Usually there is no fourth type and this command isn't used.

defunit2.text: Bonus units for local defense equal to or greater than 20 in provinces with forts only.

defunit2b.text: Second type of bonus units for local defense equal to or greater than 20 in provinces with forts.

delgod.text: Deletes a god that is otherwise gained through homerealm use.

descr.text: A full description of the nation.

disableoldnations.text: Disables all old nations (up to number 149)

disbless.text: Disables a bless effect for this nation. This blessing can't be chosen for pretender gods of this nation. NOTE: The value for all scale spread commands can be from 1-3 and indicates the maximum scale value it can raise nearby provinces to as well as the speed with which it spreads.

domdeathsense.text: Number of unburied corpses will be known where this dominion has influence.

domkill.text: The nation's Dominion kills population like Ashen Empire Ermor. Value of $10 = 1%*Dominion$ killed every month.

domsail.text: The nation's Dominion enables all units to sail like the dark vessels ability of Phaeacia.

domunrest.text: The nation's Dominion causes unrest. Unrest increase is equal to $value*0.1*dominion$ per month. Value can be negative for unrest reducing Dominions.

domwar.text: Dominion conflict bonus. Negative values can also be used to make dominion worse at spreading into enemy dominion.

dyingdom.text: Dominion is dying and needs blood sacrifice. Temples have no effect here, except if blood sacrifices are performed there or if a priest preaches there. Mictlan has a dominion like this combined with #nopreach and #sacrificedom.

earthblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

end.text: Always use this command at the end of modifying a nation.

epithet.text: Sets the epithet of a nation, e.g. Enigma of Steel for Early Era Ulm.

era.text: Which era should this nation appear in. 1 = early, 2 = mid (default), 3 = late or 0 to disable the nation. Two nations with the same name cannot be in the same era. If you change this it must be set right after #name and #epithet. Importantly descriptions and other texts will not work if the era command is too late in the mod file.

fireblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

flag.text: Replace the flag with an image. The image must be 128 pixels wide and 128 pixels high. The flag should be positioned at the bottom of this image and should usually be smaller than the entire image. A standard flag only covers about 75 percent of the height.

foreignguardcom.text: Will replace the non-foreign variant for forts that is not the capital. This command is used by Muspelheim and most nations never need it.

foreignguardmult.text: Will replace the non-foreign variant for forts that is not the capital. This command is used by Muspelheim and most nations never need it.

foreignguardunit.text: Will replace the non-foreign variant for forts that is not the capital. This command is used by Muspelheim and most nations never need it.

foreignwallcom.text: Will replace the non-foreign variant for forts that is not the capital. This command is used by Muspelheim and most nations never need it.

foreignwallmult.text: Will replace the non-foreign variant for forts that is not the capital. This command is used by Muspelheim and most nations never need it.

foreignwallunit.text: Will replace the non-foreign variant for forts that is not the capital. This command is used by Muspelheim and most nations never need it.

forestlabcost.text: Gold cost for building a lab in a forest. Default is 600.

foresttemplecost.text: Gold cost for building a temple in a forest. Default is 600.

fortcoldscaleres.text: Reduces the killing effect of cold scales in forts by this many scale steps.
