fortcost.text: Extra cost is the additional amount of gold the nation must pay for its forts, expressed as a percentage of the normal cost for building a fort. The default value is 0.

fortera.text: Determines what kind of forts the nation can build. 0 = palisades only 1 = standard forts for early era 2 = standard forts for middle era 3 = standard forts for late era 4 = better than standard forts for late era

fortheatscaleres.text: Reduces the killing effect of heat scales in forts by this many scale steps.

fortunrest.text: Unrest will increase by 1-value (open ended die roll) in all forts each month.

futuresite.text: Nation will get this site in the future, show it in nation overview. This command does not actually grant a new site, it only makes it show up in the nation overview. Some magic sites Site Effect Tar Pits 1 fire gem The Sun Below 4 fire gems Thunder Oak 1 air gem Palace of Dreams 4 air gems Weeping Stone 1 water gem Mercury Pond 2 water gems Frozen Fountain 3 water gems Mineral Cave 1 earth gem The Deepest Mine 4 earth gems Painted Cave 1 astral pearl Library of Time 4 astral pearls Burial Mound 1 death gem Well of Darkness 3 death gems Wild Forest 1 nature gem Ancient Forest 2 nature gems The Previous Forest 4 nature gems Dancing Lights 1 glamour gem Singing Tree 2 glamour gems

ghostreanim.text: Reanimating priest of this nation will create ghosts like Lemuria. NOTE: Caelian, Atlantian, Jotun, Muspel, Rephaite and monkey undead are hard coded for their respective nations and their reanimation cannot be unlocked for modding using reanimation commands.

godrebirth.text: The nation's god does not lose any magic path levels when recalled from the dead by priests.

golemhp.text: Inanimate beings in gain a percentage boost to their hit points for each dominion candle (Golem Cult dominion like Agartha).

greekreanim.text: Reanimating priest of this nation will create greek ghosts like Therodos.

guardcom.text: Commander that is in charge of the castle gate defenders. There can be multiple of these commands.

guardmult.text: Modifier for the number of castle gate guards from the previous #guardunit command. 10 is the standard amount.

guardspirit.text: Priests of this nation have a chance of receiving a guardian angel when in battle. Nbr can be negative for montags.

guardunit.text: Unit type the will guard the gates when the castle is stormed. There can be multiple of these commands, each one should be followed by a #guardmult command. The first gate guard type will also be used as city guards during assassin encounters. If there are no gate guards the first wall unit will be used instead.

halfdeathinc.text: The nation will only be half as affected by the death/growth scale regarding gold income. Abysia has this ability.

halfdeathpop.text: The nation will only be half as affected by the death/growth scale regarding population growth. Abysia has this ability.

hatesterr.text: Makes the nation less likely to start in one of the terrains in the terrain mask.

hero1.text: Gives a hero to the modded nation. A nation can have up to ten different heroes. Use monster nbr -1 to remove a hero.

hidedom.text: This dominion will hide who owns the province unless there is a scout in the province.

homecoldscaleres.text: Reduces the killing effect of cold scales in the capital by this many scale steps.

homefort.text: The nation will start with this fort in its home province. This command does not affect what type of forts the nation can build. The command is only necessary if the home fort should deviate from the standard one for their fortera. See the table below for a list of forts. homeheatscaleres.text: Reduces the killing effect of heat scales in the capital by this many scale steps.

homerealm.text: Any gods that belong to this realm (through the use of the #homerealm monster modding command) are automatically included in the nation's default list of pretenders and need not be separately added to the list with the #addgod command. See Table "Home realms". Unlike the homerealm of a pretender god, the homerealm of a nation cannot be cleared.

horsereanim.text: Reanimating priests with holy magic of level 3 or higher can reanimate longdead horsemen. Sceleria and Ashen Empire Ermor have this attribute.

idealcold.text: Sets the preferred level of cold for the nation. This ranges from -3 (very hot) to 3 (very cold).

indepflag.text: Replace the flag of independents with an image. The image must be 128 pixels wide and 128 pixels high. The flag should be positioned at the bottom of this image. This command is special in that it should be used when no nation is selected, i.e. before #selectnation or #newnation.

islandnation.text: The nation prefers to start on an island if possible, or a coast if no suitable island could be found.

islandsite.text: Like #startsite, but the nation will only get the site if it starts on an island.

killcappop.text: Kills a percentage of the capital's population when the game starts. Value can be negative to increase population instead.

labcost.text: Gold cost for building a lab. The default is 600.

likespop.text: The nation gets cheaper PD from this poptype. Can be used multiple times for different poptypes.

likesterr.text: Makes the nation more likely to start in one of the terrains in the terrain mask.

manikinreanim.text: Reanimating priest of this nation will create carrion beasts like Asphodel.

maxprison.text: Gods of this nation must not be imprisoned to more than this level. 0=awake, 1=dormant, 2=no limit.

merccost.text: Mercenaries are this much more expensive. Can be negative.

minprison.text: Gods of this nation must be imprisoned to at least this level. 0=no limit, 1=dormant, 2=imprisoned.

moregrowth.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreheat.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreluck.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moremagic.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreorder.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

moreprod.text: Alters the minimum/maximum allowed value of this scale when designing the pretender's dominion.

mountlabcost.text: Gold cost for building a lab in highlands. Default is 600.

mounttemplecost.text: Gold cost for building a temple in highlands. Default is 600.

multihero1.text: Gives a multihero to the modded nation. Use e.g. #multihero1 to set the first of seven possible multiheroes. A multihero is a hero that never runs out, i.e. there is an infinite supply of that type of hero.

name.text: Sets the name of the nation. Even though the name of a nation is changed, the file names for the 2h and trn files will be the same as the old nation’s. If the name is changed, then this must be the first command when modifying the nation.

nationinc.text: The nation will receive this much extra gold each month. The percentage value can be negative to make a nation that earn less gold.

natureblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

newnation.text: This command can be used to add a new nation instead of #selectnation. The command automatically uses the first free nation number of 120 or higher that is available.

nodeathsupply.text: A death scale does not adversely affect supplies. Abysia has this ability.

nopreach.text: Priests of this nation cannot preach. Mictlan has this disadvantage.

noundeadgods.text: This nation cannot choose any pretender that is undead. Marignon has this feature.

priestreanim.text: All priests of this nation are able to reanimate the dead as if the had the #reanimpriest attribute. They also gain the 15 points of undead leadership per holy magic level they would have received from that attribute.

recallgod.text: The nation is better at Call God than other nations. This value is added to the priest level of all priests when they perform Call God.

riverstart.text: This nation doesn't mind starting surrounded by rivers. C'tis has this ability.

sacrificedom.text: Priests of this nation can make blood sacrifices to increase dominion. Mictlan has this benefit.

seatrace.text: Can trace gold and gem income over sea provinces, like Vanheim.

secondarycolor.text: The animated background is made up of two colors, the primary color (from #color) and this one. If the secondary color is not set, it will be the same as the primary.

selectnation.text: Selects the nation that will be affected by the following modding commands. End modding this nation with the #end command. Nation number is a number between 5 and 499. See the three tables below for currently used numbers. You can use number 150 and above in order to create new nations without overwriting an existing one. Numbers 0 – 4 are used for various independents and temporary monsters in the game and cannot be used for modding. Nation numbers, Early Era Nation numbers, Middle Era Nation numbers, Late Era
values: Piconye, Legacy of the Prester King

startcom.text: The nation will start with this commander. This command also removes all old start troops and must be used when changing start units.

startscout.text: The nation will start with this unit as an extra commander. #(terrain)com "<monster name>" | <monster nbr> This commander can be recruited in (terrain) provinces with or without fort. See the box above for all terrain names. Note that "foreign" can only be used with the fortcom command. #(terrain)fortcom "<monster name>" | <monster nbr> This commander can be recruited in (terrain) provinces with a fort. See the box above for all terrain names. Note that sea, deep and kelp have no fortcom variants, use #uwrec and #uwcom instead.

startsite.text: Adds a start site for this nation. Table "Some magic sites" shows some suitable start sites. This command can be used up to 4 times for multiple start sites. Assignment by site number is not possible.

startunitnbrs1.text: The number of start units. Default is 20 units.

startunitnbrs2.text: The number of start units in the second squad. Default is 20 units.

startunittype1.text: The commander will have units of this type.

startunittype2.text: The commander will have a second squad with these units.

summary.text: A summary of the benefits and dominion themes of the nation.

supayareanim.text: Reanimating priest of this nation will create supayas like Nazca.

swamplabcost.text: Gold cost for building a lab in a swamp. Default is 600.

swamptemplecost.text: Gold cost for building a temple in a swamp. Default is 600.

syncretism.text: Syncretism enable all priests to convert conquered temples instead of demolishing them.

templecost.text: Gold cost for building a temple. Default is 600.

templegems.text: The nation's temples give gems, up to a maximum of current dominion strength. Gem type is a value from 0 to 8, same value as magic paths (0=fire, 8=blood).

templeholypoints.text: Every temple gives value number of extra holy points (for recruiting sacred units). Ind and Piconye have this ability.

templepic.text: Temple should look like this. See table below for some pic number values.

tombwyrmreanim.text: Reanimating priests can reanimate soulless of C'tis, longdead of C'tis, tomb wyrms and other special C'tissian undead. Desert Tombs C'tis has this attribute.

tradecoast.text: Income bonus for coastal forts. The nation gains more gold from coastal provinces than another nation with the same fort. Berytos has this ability. The default value is 0.

undeadreanim.text: All undead priests of this nation are able to reanimate the dead as if the had the #reanimpriest attribute.

uwbuild.text: Determines the ability of a land nation to build forts underwater. A value of 1 means yes.

uwcom.text: Add a unit to the list of recruitable commanders in underwater forts for this land-based nation. This command can be repeated multiple time for many different commanders. #landrec ”<monster name>” | <monster nbr> Add a unit to the list of recruitable units for this nation in overwater forts. Only use this command for underwater nations. #landcom ”<monster name>” | <monster nbr> Add a unit to the list of recruitable commanders for this nation in overwater forts. Only use this command for underwater nations.

uwnation.text: Underwater nation. The nation's capital is in a sea province.

uwrec.text: Add a unit to the list of recruitable units in underwater forts for this land-based nation. This command can be repeated multiple time for many different units.

uwwallcom.text: Sets wall commander for underwater forts. Works just like the overwater counterpart.

uwwallmult.text: Modifier for the number of units from the previous #uwwallunit command. Works just like the overwater counterpart.

uwwallunit.text: Sets wall defenders for underwater forts. Works just like the overwater counterpart.

viewallbat.text: This nation gets to view all battles for all players, including assassinations. This command is intended for debug or observer mods and should not be used for any real nations.

viewallprov.text: This nation gets to view all provinces regardless of owner. This command is intended for debug or observer mods and should not be used for any real nations.

wallcom.text: Commander that is in charge of the wall defenders. There can be multiple of these commands.

wallmult.text: Modifier for the number of units from the previous #wallunit command. 10 is the standard amount.

wallunit.text: Unit type the will man the walls when the castle is stormed. There can be multiple of these commands, each one should be followed by a #wallmult command.

wastelabcost.text: Gold cost for building a lab in a waste. Default is 600.

wastetemplecost.text: Gold cost for building a temple in a waste. Default is 600.

waterblessbonus.text: Gods of this nation will get extra bless design points of this type.

wightreanim.text: Reanimating priests with holy magic of level 4 or higher can reanimate undead Lictors. Ashen Empire Ermor has this attribute.

addreccom.text: Adds a commander to the recruitment list.

addrecunit.text: Adds a unit to the recruitment list.

cleardef.text: Clears province defence units from the poptype.

clearrec.text: Clears the recruitment list of all units and commanders.

defcom1.text: Sets the secondary commander for this poptype's PD when PD is 20 or higher.

defmult1.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense. E.g. #defmult1 20 will yield 2 units per point of defense, which is also the default.

defmult1b.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense for the second unit type.

defmult1c.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense for the third unit type.

defunit1.text: Sets the first type of unit in the poptype PD.

defunit1b.text: Sets the second type of unit in the poptype PD.

defunit1c.text: Sets the third type of unit in the poptype PD.

end.text: End modding each poptype with this command.

selectpoptype.text: A poptype must be selected before using any other poptype commands. Numbers from 1 to 249 are valid. See table below for poptype numbers used in the game.

adventureruin.text: A commander who enters the ruin has a chance to discover gold, gems, magic items or other rewards. Those who fail may fall victim to lethal traps or bloodthirsty monsters.

airrange.text: All Air rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

allrange.text: All magic rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

altcost.text: All rituals of the Alteration school cast in this province cost <bonus> % less to cast.

astralrange.text: All Astral rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

blessairshld.text: Blessed troops get Air Shield like from an Air bless. An existing Air bless is augmented.

blessanimawe.text: Blessed troops get Animal Awe. An existing Animal Awe ability is augmented.

blessatt.text: Blessed troops get increased Attack skill.

blessawe.text: Blessed troops get Awe. An existing Awe ability is augmented.

blesscoldres.text: Blessed troops get increased Cold Resistance.

blessdarkvis.text: Blessed troops get Darkvision. An existing Darkvision ability is augmented.

blessdef.text: Blessed troops get increased Defense skill.

blessdtv.text: Blessed troops get undying, like the undying bless effect. An existing undying bless is augmented.

blessfireres.text: Blessed troops get increased Fire Resistance.

blesshp.text: Blessed troops get increased Hit Points.

blessmr.text: Blessed troops get increased Magic Resistance.

blesspoisres.text: Blessed troops get increased Poison Resistance.

blessprec.text: Blessed troops get increased Precision skill.

blessreinvig.text: Blessed troops get increased Reinvigoration, like from a bless with the same name. An existing reinvigoration bless is augmented.

blessshockres.text: Blessed troops get increased Shock Resistance.

bloodcost.text: All rituals of the Blood Magic school cast in this province cost <bonus> % less to cast.

bloodrange.text: All Blood rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

claim.text: The effects of magic site commands that appear after this command are not active until the throne is claimed by a god, a disciple, a prophet or a priest with Holy level 3 or higher. If you modify an already existing throne there is no need to add this command, all effects will be put after a claim requirment that is already there (unless you clear the site).

clear.text: Clears the attributes of the selected magic site.

cluster.text: Assigns a cluster value to a throne. A throne is likely to appear together with other thrones of same cluster value when a map is created. For example, the Throne of Spring and the Throne of Autumn have the same cluster value and if one of them appears on the map, the other is also very likely to appear. Cluster value can be a number from 1 to 32000.

com.text: Adds a monster that can be recruited as commander by the owner of this site.

conjcost.text: All rituals of the Conjuration school cast in this province cost <bonus> % less to cast.

constcost.text: All rituals of the Construction school cast in this province cost <bonus> % less to cast.

copysite.text: Copies all site stats from this site, including name.

curse.text: Every turn any unit in the province has the indicated chance (percent) to become cursed.

deathrange.text: All Death rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

decscale.text: Decreases the selected scale by one point per turn to a maximum of -3 / 3. This command functions as #incscale for the opposite scales.

decunrest.text: The site decreases unrest in the province. The value can be negative in order to increase unrest.

defcom.text: Extra commander for province defense. This will be in addition to the normal defence.

defmult.text: Number of units per 10 points of defense. Default is 10.

defunit.text: Extra units for province defense. This will be in addition to the normal defence.

disease.text: Every turn any unit in the province has the indicated chance (percent) to become diseased.

dominion.text: The site will spread the god's dominion by automatically initiating a number of temple checks per month.

earthrange.text: All Earth rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

elementrange.text: All Elemental magic (Fire, Air, Water, Earth) rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

enchcost.text: All rituals of the Enchantment school cast in this province cost <bonus> % less to cast.

end.text: Always use this command at the end of modifying a site.

evil.text: The throne is evil and is likely to be defended by evil monsters.

evocost.text: All rituals of the Evocation school cast in this province cost <bonus> % less to cast.

firerange.text: All Fire rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

fort.text: Constructs a fort in the province when the site is discovered. If a fort is already present, there is no effect. If a fort is under construction, the construction is canceled and the fort discovered by the site is constructed immediately instead. See table <<-1 for a list of forts.

gems.text: Gives gem income to the magic site. Path should be a number between 0 and 8. See table <<-1.

glamourrange.text: All Glamour rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

goddomchaos.text: Increases the Turmoil or chaos scale of the god's dominion. Use a negative value to increase Order.

goddomcold.text: Increases the Cold scale of the god's dominion. Use a negative value to increase Heat.

goddomdeath.text: Increases the Death scale of the god's dominion. Use a negative value to increase Growth.

goddomdrain.text: Increases the Drain scale of the god's dominion. Use a negative value to increase Magic.

goddomlazy.text: Increases the Sloth scale of the god's dominion. Use a negative value to increase Production.

goddommisfortune.text: Increases the Misfortune scale of the god's dominion. Use negative value to increase Luck.

gold.text: Adds a gold income to the site.

heal.text: The site causes a healing check to be performed at the indicated percent chance on every unit in the province, like a healing unit set to Heal Troops. If the healing check is successful, a check against the healing difficulty of any affliction the unit has is performed. If the difficulty check is successful, up to one affliction is removed.

holyfire.text: Every turn any undead or demonic troops in the province have the indicated chance (percent) to be struck by holy fire, which deals 10 points of armor-negating damage if they fail a MR check against an attack value of 12.

holypower.text: Every turn any undead troops in the province have the indicated chance (percent) to be struck by holy power, which deals 10 points of armor- negating damage if they fail a MR check against an attack value of 12.

homecom.text: Adds a monster that can be recruited as commander by the original owner of this site only.

homemon.text: Adds a monster that can be recruited by the original owner of this site only.

horrormark.text: Every turn any unit in the province has the indicated chance (percent) to be horror marked.

incscale.text: Increases the selected scale by one point per turn to a maximum of -3 / 3. This command functions as #decscale for the opposite scales.

lab.text: Constructs a lab in the province when the site is discovered. If a lab is already present, there is no effect.

level.text: Level should be a number between 0 and 4 and is the level of magic required to find the site. Level 0 sites are automatically discovered.

loc.text: This command can restrict the random placement of a site to certain terrains or flag the site as unique. Useful numbers are 735 for a site that can be located in any land province (default) and 288 for sites that can be located in any sea. Locmask 1023 means a site can appear in any province, land or sea. You can calculate your own locmask by adding all the places your site is allowed to appear in on Table 27. The value Unique is special and indicates that there can only be one of that site in a given world unless also scripted in a map file.

look.text: Set what the site should look like. Site spr -1 = default look, 0-9 = specific sprite (for some paths not all 9 are available and the last ones will look the same).

mon.text: Adds a monster that can be recruited by the owner of this site.

name.text: This sets the name of the site.

nat.text: Sets the nation for the following two commands.

natcom.text: Adds a monster that can be recruited as commander if the site is owned by the nation set by the #nat command.

natmon.text: Adds a monster that can be recruited if the site is owned by the nation set by the #nat command.

naturerange.text: All Nature rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

newsite.text: Site nbr (optional) should be a number between 1700 and 3999. It must not be the same as any other site. This new site will be affected by the following modding commands and there should be an #end command at the end. It is recommended not to use a site number for sites with a unique name, because this will lessen the risk of conflicts between mods.

path.text: The magic path associated with this site.

popgrowth.text: Bonus to population growth in province once site has been found.

rarity.text: Rarity should be 0 for common, 1 for uncommon, 2 for rare and 5 for sites that are never used as a random site. Rarity 11-13 means a Throne of Ascension of level 1-3.

recallgod.text: This value is added to the priest level of everyone doing Call God.

res.text: Adds a resource bonus to the site.

scry.text: A mage with the same path as the site may enter to scry a distant province. The scrying is a magic ritual which provides accurate scouting information on the province for <duration> turns and reveals the icons for revealed magic sites. Site names or other properties are not shown.

scryrange.text: Set the maximum range of the scry ability. If not set a maximum range of 6 provinces will be used.

selectsite.text: Selects the magic site that will be affected by the following modding commands. End modding this site with the #end command.

sorceryrange.text: All Sorcery magic (Astral, Death, Nature, Blood) rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

summon.text: A mage of the same magic path as the site may enter to summon the specified monster. To summon more than one monster of the same type, the command must be used multiple times.

summonlvl2.text: Like #summon, except that the mage summoning must be at least level 2.

summonlvl3.text: Like #summon, except that the mage summoning must be at least level 3.

summonlvl4.text: Like #summon, except that the mage summoning must be at least level 4.

supply.text: The magic site provides <value> supplies to the province where it is located.

temple.text: Constructs a temple in the province when the site is discovered. If a temple is already present, there is no effect.

thaucost.text: All rituals of the Thaumaturgy school cast in this province cost <bonus> % less to cast.

uwwallcom.text: Adds to castle defenders. Works just like the nation modding command with the same name.

uwwallmult.text: Adds to castle defenders. Works just like the nation modding command with the same name.

uwwallunit.text: Adds to castle defenders. Works just like the nation modding command with the same name.

voidgate.text: A mage with the same path as the site may enter to summon Void creatures. Void Summoning skill increases the success chance. A mage who does not have the Voidsanity attribute may become insane or feebleminded.

wallcom.text: Adds to castle defenders. Works just like the nation modding command with the same name.

wallmult.text: Adds to castle defenders. Works just like the nation modding command with the same name.

wallunit.text: Adds to castle defenders. Works just like the nation modding command with the same name.

waterrange.text: All Water rituals cast in this province have their range increased by <range boost> provinces.

wild.text: The throne is wild and is likely to be defended by wild monsters.

xp.text: A commander may enter the site to gain <value> experience points per turn for himself and all troops under his command.

end.text: Always use this command at the end of modifying a sample.

loop.text: This should be -1 for sound effects, -2 for music, -4 for battle music and -5 for the intro tune. A postitive number means the sample will loop to the sample with that number after finishing (this is never used in Dominions). sample.text: Imports the sound from this sound file.

selectsound.text: Selects an existing or a new sample (sound effect or background music) that will be affected by the following modding commands. End modding this sample with the #end command. Number 150+ can be used to add new samples for mods. The highest number that can be used is 248.

smpmode.text: Mode should be 0 for standard sound effect and 2 for music. Sound effects can also use number 3-5. 3=less random pitch, 4=no random pitch, 5=extra random pitch.

aiassmod.text: This modifies the spell AI to (dis)like this spell when in an assassination battle. Usually there is no need for this command. A value of -100 makes it never be cast and a value of 100 makes it twice as likable for the spell AI.

aibadlvl.text: The spell AI will never choose this spell if is is level or higher in the required magic path.

ainocast.text: The spell AI will never select this spell unless it has been scripted. Use this for spells like Returning that should normally never be cast.

aispellmod.text: This modifies the spell AI to (dis)like this spell. Usually there is no need for this command. A value of -50 makes it half as likable for the spell AI and a value of 100 makes it twice as likable for the spell AI. The value can be between -100 and 1000, a value of -100 will make it never be cast, even if scripted to cast it.

aoe.text: Sets the area of effect for this spell. Add 1000 to this value to give larger areas to more powerful casters. E.g. 1001 means area = 1+1/level of caster (area would be 2 for a level 1 mage). A value of 666 means that the entire battlefield is affected. 663 means that 50% of all squares are affected, 665 = 25%, 664 = 10%, 662 = 5%.

casttime.text: Set the casting time of a spell, the casting time is 100 for a standard spell. There is usually no need to set this value as Dominions will automatically give certain spells like battle enchantments higher casting time to fit in with all the other spells.

clearallspells.text: All researchable spells are removed from the game.

copyspell.text: Copies all stats including name from the specified spell to the current spell.

cure.text: This is the part of the dire portent message that is only sent to the enemies of the caster. It can use the same special tags. Dire portent tags ##fullgodname## ##godname## ##disname## ##fullplayername## ##playername## ##playergodname## ##fullplayergodname## ##godhe## ##dishe## ##godhis## ##godHis## ##dishis## ##disHis## ##godhim## ##dishim## ##godhimself## ##dishimself## ##godthrone## ##playerthrone## ##playergodthrone## ##godnat## ##disnat## Tags that contain "god" references the caster's god. Those that contain "dis" references the nation's leader, this can be a disciple or a god. The tag "player" references the player that is receiving the message.

damage.text: Set the damage for this spell. Add 1000 to dmg to make the damage be variable with the level of the caster. Damage means damage for damage spells, but it can also mean many other things for different spells. E.g. summoning spells use this value to determine which monster is summoned.

damagemon.text: Use this to set a spell's damage to a monster if you don't know its number.

descr.text: A text description of the spell.

details.text: This command is not necessary. If used it will set the yellow spell detail text under the main spell description.

dispimmune.text: This command will make an enchantment immune to dispels. This command works for both local and global enchentments. 1 = immune to astral disruption only, 2 = immune to all dispels.

effect.text: Set the effect of the spell. Some of the most common eff values can be seen in tables "Ritual spell effects" and "Combat spell effects". Value higher than 10000 are rituals and those lower are combat spells. There are many other values that can be used, but these are the only documented ones for now. Press ctrl-i in game when viewing the spell details to see some modding information including the effect value.

end.text: Always use this command at the end of modifying a spell. Nbr School – 1 cannot be researched 0 Conjuration 1 Alteration 2 Evocation 3 Construction 4 Enchantment 5 Thaumaturgy 6 Blood 7 Divine

explspr.text: Set the particle effect to be used when this spell explodes. -1 = no explosion. See table "Explosion fx" to find a suitable explosion.

farsumcom.text: Sets the commander for farsummoned units to something other than the normal units.

fatiguecost.text: Set the fatigue cost for this spell. Every 100 in fatigue cost raises the required number of gems or blood slaves by one. Must be used also for rituals to set their gem cost.

flightspr.text: Set the sprite or particle effect to be used when this spell is flying. The flysprite nbr should be a value from the table "Flysprites".

friendlyench.text: 1 means the enchantment created by this spell is friendly. It will be dispelled automatically if the province is conquered by the enemy.

globallook.text: If global should be visible from map (localglobal only) this command can be used to determine what it should look like. Values for globallook 1 Eternal Pyre 2 Mother Oak 3 Well of Misery 4 Stellar Focus 5 Maelstrom 6 Blood Vortex 7 Winds of Parched Magic 8 Gates of Horn and Ivory 9 Earthblood Deepwell

godpathspell.text: This is used for divine spells that should only be available when the God is best with this particular magic path. -1 can be used for the fallback spell that should be available when the god has no path that is good enough.

hiddenench.text: 1 means the enchantment created by this spell is not visible during battles. It should be used on enchantments that does not affect battles.

homerealm.text: Restrict the spell to nations belonging to a certain home realm.

localglobal.text: This is a localized global enchantment. It will have its origin in the province where it was cast.

makecrater.text: Makes a crater where it lands.

maxbounces.text: Set the maximum number of bounces for a chain lightning (effect 134) type of spell effect.

name.text: Sets the name for the active spell. Changing name of a spell will also remove its description, so make sure to set name before description. 38

napbreakrit.text: A positive value means the ritual counts as a NAP violation. A negative value means it will never count as a NAP violation.

newspell.text: Creates a new spell and selects it for modding by the following commands. End creating the spell with the #end command.

nextingeo.text: The spell after this will also take effect if it cast in this terrain. For combat spells only.

nextspell.text: With this command the effect of another spell will also take place when the effect of the main spell occurs. The nextspell takes place on every area where the main spell takes effect. So make sure the area of the second spell isn’t greater than 1 or there will be overlaps.

nocastmindless.text: 1 means mindless units cannot cast this spell.

nogeodst.text: Ritual cannot target provinces with any of these terrains. See table "Terrain masks". Only used for spells that target faraway provinces.

nogeosrc.args: <terrain mask>__ Spell or ritual cannot be cast
nogeosrc.text: from any of these terrains. See table "Terrain masks".

nolandtrace.text: 1 = ritual range cannot trace over land. 0 = ritual range can trace over land (default)

notfornation.text: Restricts a spell so that it cannot be used by this nation. This command can be used multiple times on the same spell.

notindoors.text: 1 = cannot be cast indoors, -1 = can be cast indoors, even it it usually should not be castable there. Battlefield enchantments and other battlefield wide spells cannot be cast indoors by default.

notmnr.text: This type of monster is unable to cast this spell. Monster nbr can be negative for a montag. This command can be used multiple times on the same spell for non-montags.

nowatertrace.text: 1 = ritual range cannot trace through water provinces. 0 = Ritual range can trace through water provinces (default)

nreff.text: Sets the number of effects for this spell. For summoning spells this determines how many creatures are summoned. Add 1000, 2000 or 3000 to this value to give more powerful casters more effects. Every 1000 gives one additional effect for every level of the caster. Add 500 instead to give one extra effect for every two levels the caster exceeds the requirement of the spell.

onlyatsite.text: Ritual can only be cast in provinces containing this site.

onlycoastsrc.text: 1 means this ritual can only be cast from a coast province.

onlyfriendlydst.text: 1 = can only target allied provinces, 2 = can also target allied forts even when besieged.

onlygeodst.text: Ranged ritual can only target one of these terrains. See table "Terrain masks". Only used for spells that target faraway provinces.

onlygeosrc.text: Spell or ritual can only be cast from one of these terrains. See table "Terrain masks" for possible terrain mask values. 2^x Nbr Terrain -0 Plains 0 1 Small Province 1 2 Large Province 2 4 Sea 3 8 Freshwater 4 16 Mountain 5 32 Swamp 6 64 Waste 7 128 Forest 8 256 Farm 9 512 Nostart 10 1024 Many Sites 11 2048 Deep Sea 12 4096 Cave 23 8388608 Border Mountain

onlymnr.text: Only this type of monster is able to cast this spell. Monster nbr can be negative for a montag. This command can be used multiple times on the same spell for non-montags.

onlyowndst.text: 1 = can only target own provinces. 0 = can target any province (default)

onlysitedst.text: Ritual can only target provinces containing this site. The site must be revealed to be targetted.

path.text: The path of the spell. Reqnr should be 0 for the first required path and 1 for the second required path. The path nbr should be a number between -1 and 9, see table "Magic path numbers for spells".

pathlevel.text: Level required to cast this spell. Magic path numbers for spells

polygetmagic.text: 1 means a unit polymorphed by this ritual will get the magic of the target creature.

portent.text: Global enchantments come with a "dire portent" message to all players. This command can be used to set the part of the text that is sent to all players. Don't write "A dire portent..." that part is added at the start automatically. Special tags shown in the table below can be inserted in the message to reference things like the name of the caster's god.

precision.text: Set the precision for this spell.

provrange.text: Sets the range of a ritual in provinces.

range.text: Sets the battlefield range for this spell. Add 5000 to this value to give longer range (5 extra per level) to more powerful casters.

reqnoplant.text: Trees and plants cannot cast this spell.

reqnoseduce.text: Units with the seduce ability cannot cast this spell.

reqnospellsinger.text: Units with the spell singing ability cannot cast this spell.

reqnotaskmaster.text: Units with the task master ability cannot cast this spell.

reqplant.text: Only trees and plants can cast this spell.

reqseduce.text: Only units with the seduce ability can cast this spell.

reqspellsinger.text: Only units with the spell singing ability can cast this spell.

reqsun.text: This command can make a combat spell uncastable when there is no sun present. A sun is usually not present in caves, deep seas and during the night.

reqtaskmaster.text: Only units with the task master ability can cast this spell.

researchlevel.text: Level of research required to learn this spell. The level should be a number between 0 and 9.

restricted.text: Spell will only be available for this nation. You can use up to 12 of these commands for a single spell, thus enabling up to 12 nations to research the spell. A value of -1 restricts the spell to the last manipulated nation, so this command can be used with #newnation. The number of times this command can be used on a single spell is also somewhat dependent on how many other things the spell does, so limiting the use of this command to less than the total number allowed is advised.

sample.text: Uses this sample as sound effect for when the spell is cast. The sample must be in .sw (16-bit signed words, 22050 Hz, mono) or .al (a-law, 22050 Hz, mono) format. This command can also be used for weapons.

school.text: Magic school for this spell. The number ranges from -1 to 7, see Table "Magic schools".

selectspell.text: Selects an existing spell that will be affected by the following modding commands. End modding this spell with the #end command.

sethome.text: The commander casting this ritual will get his home province set to the current province.

sizecost.text: Units that are not human sized will have the cost of the ritual adjusted by (value)*(size difference). Cost will never go below zero.

sound.text: The sample that will sound when this spell is cast. Samples have the same number as the weapon samples, see table "Sound effects".

spec.text: Sets the special abilities of a spell. 8388608 is a useful number and it means that the spell can be cast under water. 64 is armor piercing, 128 is armor negating and 4096 means MR negates. Add values together to make combinations.
values: Does not affect the caster or his mount
More likely to hit in the head (75%)

speedmult.text: Use this command to make the spell projectiles fly slower or faster. By default spell projectiles have a speed of 1.

spellreqfly.text: 1 means only flying units can cast this ritual.

strikesound.text: The sample that will sound when this spell strikes down. Samples have the same number as the weapon samples, see table "Sound effects".

sumhealaffs.text: Units summoned by this spell will have up to value number of afflictions healed. This can be useful if summoning an immortal or unique monster that might have accumulated afflictions in its previous life.

twiceborncost.text: Units that are not human sized after being transformed by the twiceborn ritual will have the cost of the ritual adjusted by (value)*(size difference after twiceborn). Cost will never go below zero.

walkable.text: 1 = ritual range must trace along a walkable path. 0 = ritual range need not be walkable (default)

worldvisible.text: This enchantment can be seen from all over the world. Use together with #localglobal.

bless.text: The bless effects for this pretender.

end.text: Always put this command last, after all commands belonging to the new template.

favrit.text: Makes the AI prioritize casting this ritual or forging this magic item. Many favrit commands can be used to make the AI prioritize multiple things. Disschool and level can be set to -1,-1 to never disable this favorite. Otherwise school should be a spell school and level a research level, when the AI reaches this the command will be disabled.

form.text: The physical form of the pretender. Optionally the monster name can end with the monster number in parentesis, like "Dragon (265)" to distinguish between different monsters of the same name.

newtemplate.text: Always start a new template with this command. It creates a new template for a specific nation.

researchgoal.text: This will make the AI research to get access to this spell or magic item. Many researchgoal can be set, in which case the AI will research to get them in that order. The AI's research might not be exactly like ordered, but it will mostly follow the plans.

scale.text: Scales are numbered from 0-5 and they can have values of -5 to 5.

acid.text: This weapon does acid damage. Acid weapons can damage armor. Damaged armor will break if subjected to more blows, but will be repaired if there are enough resources in the province the monster is in.

aftercloud.text: A cloud will appear after attacking with the weapon. The cloud has strength "cloudstr" and is of the "cloudnbr> type. See table below for possible cloud types.

aftercloudarea.text: Size of the aftercloud effect of this weapon. Default is 1.

ammo.text: <ammo> This is the number of times that this weapon can be fired in combat. The default value is 12. The maximum value for normal ammunition is 30. Values over 1000 means fatigue cost instead of limited ammunition, the cost per attack is this value minus 1000.

aoe.text: This is the area of effect in squares. A value of zero (default) means that only one opponent will be affected. A value of one or more indicates the number of squares that will be affected. An area of two or more squares is large enough that the user of this weapon might hit himself as well.

armornegating.text: The weapon is armor negating. Armor is completely ignored when determining damage.

armorpiercing.text: The weapon is armor piercing. Armor protection is halved when determining damage.

att.text: Sets the attack value of the weapon. A spear has an attack value of 0 and a sword has 1. This value is also used as precision for missile weapons.

blunt.text: The weapon does blunt damage. Monsters with Blunt Resistance only take half damage.

bonus.text: This is an intrinsic weapon that will not incur a multiple weapon penalty or get replaced when the commander is equipped with a magic weapon item. If a monster doesn't have any hands to hold weapons, it should only have bonus weapons. Monsters without hand slots risk getting all non-bonus weapons disabled.

bowstr.text: This is the same as the #thirdstr command. It is an old command that was used for bows in Dominions 5.

charge.text: The weapon will receive a damage bonus on its first attack. This bonus is proportional to the unit’s maximum number of action points.

cold.text: This weapon does cold damage. A cold resistant being will take reduced damage from this weapon.

copyweapon.text: Copies all stats from an existing weapon. This command will overwrite all stats for the selected weapon, so it should be used as the first command after the #newweapon command.

def.text: Sets the defense value of the weapon. A spear has a defense value of 0 and a sword has 1.

defroll.text: If the victim passes a defence roll vs 3d6, there will be no effect.

demononly.text: The weapon only causes affects demons.

demonundead.text: The weapon only affects demons and undead.

dmg.text: Sets the damage value of the weapon. A spear has a damage value of 3 and a sword has 6.

dt_aff.text: Sets the damage type of the weapon to a special effect or affliction. The specific affliction the weapon inflicts is set with the #dmg command, so the weapon's damage value is interpreted as a bitmask value according to the (affliction table)(#afflictions). The table uses bitmask values, meaning powers of 2. The numbers are expressed as powers of 2, because numbers after about 2^20 get very big very quickly. For example, in order to make a weapon inflict plague (3), you must enter the value of 2^3 as an argument to #dmg in order to get the correct result. In this case the correct value would be 8. and the mod code would look like this, for example: #newweapon 1200

dt_bouncekill.text: This effect will bounce a few times to nearby targets, like a chain lightning. Weapons with this effect should have aoe = 1.

dt_cap.text: Sets the damage type to capped damage (max 1 HP damage) like a whip or a blowgun.

dt_constructonly.text: Only inanimate beings are affected by this weapon.

dt_demon.text: Sets the damage type to anti-demon damage. This means double damage to demons.

dt_drain.text: The weapon drains life force from its target, healing damage and reducing fatigue for the attacker.

dt_holy.text: Sets the damage type to holy damage. This means triple damage to undead and demons.

dt_interrupt.text: This damage is not real, but it can still interrupt mages casting spells.

dt_large.text: The weapon does triple damage against creatures larger than the attacker.

dt_magic.text: The weapon does double damage to magic beings.

dt_normal.text: Sets the damage type to normal damage. This is the default.

dt_paralyze.text: Sets the damage type to paralyze. Damage value is NOT directly turns of paralysis. Use 10 for a standard strength paralyze.

dt_poison.text: Sets the damage delivery mechanism to poison damage. Poison damage is caused over several combat rounds. To make a poisoned weapon, do NOT use this command. Use a secondary effect that has both #poison and this command.

dt_raise.text: If the target is killed by the weapon, it is animated as a soulless servant of the attacker.

dt_realstun.text: Sets the damage type to stun. The damage value for stun weapons should be 100. Stunned units are unable to take any action for about 1 combat round.

dt_sizestun.text: Sets the damage type to fatigue damage that is less effective on large targets. Effectively the same as #dt_stun + #sizeresist.

dt_small.text: The weapon does double damage against creatures smaller than the attacker.

dt_stun.text: Sets the damage type to fatigue damage.

dt_weakness.text: The weapon drains strength from its target instead of doing normal damage.

dt_weapondrain.text: The weapon drains life, but max 5 points of the damage is used to heal the wielder. Use this for draining weapons that can be wielded or forged.

end.text: Gives poison immune beings immunity to this weapon. For example, Poison Sling and Snake Bladder Stick both have this attribute and the #dt_poison attribute.

enemyimmune.text: Enemy units are immune to this weapon.

explspr.text: Use this command to set how the explosion looks like when a missile hits something or when a melee weapon strikes. Table Explosion fx shows some numbers that can be used. Any number between 10001 and 10317 can be used. Use number -1 to disable an explosion effect. false.text: The weapon causes false damage (like most glamour magic) instead of real damage.

fire.text: This weapon does fire damage. A fire resistant being will take reduced damage from this weapon.

flail.text: The weapon has a +2 attack bonus against shields. Morningstars and flails have this feature. Whips do not, because they do not have enough momentum when they wrap around a shield.

flyingimmune.text: Flying and floating beings are immune to this weapon.

flyspr.text: Use this command to set how the arrow looks like for a missile weapon. A value of -1 for a flysprite means there is no flysprite at all. Table Flysprites some numbers that can be used for missile weapons. Flysprite numbers of 10000 and higher are particle effects, lower numbers are hand drawn sprites.

friendlyimmune.text: Friendly units are immune to this weapon.

fullstr.text: The full weapon wielder's strength will be added to the damage. This is the default and need not be specified.

halfstr.text: Only one half of the weapon wielder's strength will be added to the damage. This is normally used for bows, slings and the breath weapons of dragons.

hardmrneg.text: The effects of the weapon may be resisted by MR, but there is a penalty to the MR check.

holyifhit.text: AN damage that only affect demons and undeads.

holystunifhit.text: Stun that only affects demons and undead. Use 1 as damage value.

iceweapon.text: The weapon is made of ice and cannot be fire blessed.

illusionsimmune.text: Illusions are immune to this weapon.

inanimateimmune.text: Lifeless beings are immune to this weapon.

internal.text: The weapon inflicts internal damage that cannot be negated by effects like mist form, mossbody, etc. Used on e.g. Incinerate and Disintegrate.

ironweapon.text: The weapon is made of iron and is subject to rust and spells that damage iron equipment.

killdemonifhit.text: AN damage that only affect demons.

killmagicifhit.text: AN damage that only affect magic beings.

len.text: Sets the length of the weapon. This should be a value between 0 (fist) and 5 (pike). A spear has a value of 3 and a sword 1.

magic.text: This is a magic weapon that can harm ethereal units with ease.

magiconly.text: The weapon only affects magic beings.

melee50.text: This melee weapon only has 50% chance of being used.

mind.text: Mindless beings are immune to this weapon.

morroll.text: If the victim passes a morale roll vs 3d6, there will be no effect.

mrhalf.text: A successful MR check will halve the damage received from this attack.

mrnegates.text: The effects of the weapon can be resisted by MR.

mrnegateseasily.text: The effects of the weapon can be easily resisted by MR.

name.text: This must be the first command for every new weapon. It sets the name of the weapon.

natural.text: Marks the weapon as a natural ranged weapon. Use this for things like breath weapons or mind blasts. Weapons with this attribute will not be affected by blesses like fire weapons.

newweapon.text: Weapon number for new weapons should be a number between 1000 and 3999. It must not be the same as any other weapon. This new weapon will be affected by the following modding commands and there should be an #end command at the end.

norepel.text: This weapon cannot be used to repel attacks.

nostr.text: The strength of the weapon wielder will not be added to the damage.

notdismounted.text: This weapon cannot be used while dismounted.

notmounted.text: This weapon cannot be used while mounted (2=keep this secret and don't show it in weapon info).

nouw.text: This ranged weapon cannot be used underwater. This is the default property of all ranged weapons, but the command can be used to remove the ability to fire underwater from an existing ranged weapon (e.g. lightning, mind blast or ethereal crossbow).

nratt.text: Sets the number of attacks per round for a weapon. For slow missile weapons set this value to -2 for every other round or -3 for every third round.

pierce.text: The weapon does piercing damage. Monsters with Pierce Resistance only take half damage.

poison.text: Gives poison immune beings immunity to this weapon. For example, Poison Sling and Snake Bladder Stick both have this attribute and the #dt_poison attribute.

poisonifdmg.text: AN poison damage. Clouds will appear after the weapon has been swung regardless of hit or miss. Cloud strength can vary from 1 to 7, all auras in the game have strength 1, but weapons often result in more powerful clouds.

range.text: <range> Sets the maximum firing range for a missile weapon. This command also turns the weapon into a missile weapon that cannot be used in melee combat. A short bow has a range of 35. A value of -1 sets the weapon range to equal the strength of the monster (like a javelin), -2 to strength/2, -3 to strength/3, etc.

range0.text: This ranged weapon can also be used in melee.

range050.text: This ranged weapon has a 50% chance of being used in melee.

rcost.text: <resources> Sets the resource cost for the weapon. Default value is 0, a spear costs 1 resource and a sword costs 3.

sacredonly.text: The weapon only affects sacred troops.

sample.text: "filename" Uses this sample as sound effect. The sample must be in .sw (16-bit signed words, 22050 Hz, mono) or .al (a-law, 22050 Hz, mono) format. This command can also be used for spells.

secondaryeffect.text: This secondary effect will affect anyone harmed by the weapon. See Table secondary weapon effects on page <<-1 for some premade effects. The effects are also weapons and share the same numbers as all other weapons and you can create a new secondary effect by creating a new weapon.

secondaryeffectalways.text: This secondary effect will affect anyone attacked by the weapon, no matter if it was a hit or not, as long as the secondary effect itself has an area of effect of one or greater. If the secondary effect does not have an area of effect, it will activate when the target is hit, even if actual damage is not inflicted. See table secondary weapon effects on page <<-1 for some premade effects. Only one of #secondaryeffectalways and #secondaryeffect can be used. You must use the always variant with area effects. For non-area effects either one can be used, but you usually want the non-always variant for these weapons.

selectweapon.text: Selects the weapon that will be affected by the following modding commands. End modding this weapon with the #end command. To find out the numbers of a particular unit’s weapons, look at the unit’s stats in the game and press ctrl+i.

shock.text: This weapon does shock damage. A shock resistant being will take reduced damage from this weapon.

shockifhit.text: AN shock damage. These effects that will take effect once someone is wounded by the weapon. It is also possible to make these effects using secondary effects, this way is just more convenient as these effects are quite common.

sizeresist.text: Units that are size 3 or 4 have a chance of resisting the effects of the weapon. Size 5+ units always resist the effects and size 1 and 2 units never resist the effect. Str 15+ also has a chance to resist and Str 35+ always resists.

skip.text: Once this weapon is used, skip the next weapon.

skip2.text: Once this weapon is used, skip the next 2 weapons.

slash.text: The weapon does slashing damage. Monsters with Slash Resistance only take half damage.

sound.text: The sound effect that will be played when this weapon strikes. Some commonly used sounds can be found in the sound effects table. spiritformimmune.text: Spiritform beings and illusions are immune to this weapon.

thirdstr.text: Only one third of the weapon wielder's strength will be added to the damage. This is normally used for crossbows.

twohanded.text: Makes the weapon a two-handed weapon. This means the weapon cannot be combined with a shield if you have only two arms. Two-handed weapons also receive increased bonus damage from strength.

undeadimmune.text: Undead beings are immune to this weapon.

uwok.text: This ranged weapon can be used underwater and is not affected by storms.
